stem: DreamHouse Realty has a policy that requires the phone number on Contact to be deleted when the Do Not Call checkbox is checked. Which automation tool should the app builder recommend?
sourceExplanation: Flow is the correct automation tool because it can automatically update records based on specific conditions. A record-triggered flow can detect when the Do Not Call checkbox on a Contact is checked and then clear (delete) the Phone field without any user action. This meets the policy requirement to enforce data changes automatically. Why the other options are incorrect: If-then rule: This is not an actual Salesforce automation feature and cannot be used to enforce data changes. Validation rule: Validation rules only prevent a record from being saved if conditions are not met. They cannot modify or delete field values such as the Phone number. Quick action: Quick actions require manual user interaction. Since the requirement is automatic enforcement when the checkbox is checked, a quick action is not appropriate.

stem: A production org includes custom objects containing confidential information. A sandbox is needed that includes data records, excludes all of the Confidential objects, and can be refreshed weekly. Which steps should an app builder take to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a Developer Pro Sandbox and schedule Data Loader to download selected object data weekly.
Create a Full Copy Sandbox and use a sandbox template.
Create a Partial Copy Sandbox and use a sandbox template.
Create a Developer Sandbox and schedule Data Loader to download selected object data weekly.

sourceExplanation: Create a Partial Copy Sandbox and use a sandbox template is the correct approach because a Partial Copy Sandbox can include data records while allowing the app builder to control exactly which objects are copied. By using a sandbox template, the builder can explicitly exclude all Confidential custom objects. Partial Copy sandboxes also support regular refreshes, including weekly refresh cycles, which meets all stated requirements. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a Developer Pro Sandbox and schedule Data Loader to download selected object data weekly: Developer Pro sandboxes do not include production data by default. Manually loading data with Data Loader adds unnecessary complexity and does not inherently enforce the exclusion of confidential objects during refresh. Create a Full Copy Sandbox and use a sandbox template: Full Copy sandboxes include all production data, including confidential information. Even with a sandbox template, Full Copy sandboxes are refreshed less frequently and are not designed for weekly refreshes. Create a Developer Sandbox and schedule Data Loader to download selected object data weekly: Developer sandboxes do not contain production data and have limited storage. Relying on Data Loader does not meet the requirement for automated, controlled data inclusion and weekly refresh behavior.

stem: Universal Containers wants sales reps to get permission from their managers before deleting Opportunities. What can be used to meet these requirements?

options.text: Approval process and flow with a scheduled path
Schedule-triggered flow with Submit for Approval action
Approval process with a record triggered flow

sourceExplanation: Approval process with a record-triggered flow is the correct solution because Salesforce does not natively support approvals for delete actions. A record-triggered flow can intercept the delete attempt (before delete), prevent the deletion, and submit the Opportunity for approval. Once a manager approves, the flow can then allow or perform the deletion through controlled automation. This approach ensures sales reps must obtain manager permission before an Opportunity is deleted. Why the other options are incorrect: Two-step approval process: Approval processes alone cannot control or approve record deletions. They are designed for record updates, not delete actions. Approval process and flow with a scheduled path: Scheduled paths are time-based and are not suitable for intercepting or controlling delete operations, which must occur immediately. Schedule-triggered flow with Submit for Approval action: Schedule-triggered flows run at a specific time and cannot respond to a user’s real-time delete action.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants the field sales team to only see the accounts that they Own. Separate North American and European marketing teams should only see Accounts in their respective regions. The inside sales team needs to see all accounts In Salesforce. How can this be accomplished?

options.text: Set the Organization-Wide Default to Public for accounts. Create profiles for each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team role that is at the top of the Role Hierarchy.

Set the Organization Wide Default to Public for accounts. Create criteria-based sharing rules for Each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team permission set with the "View All" setting for Accounts.
Set the Organization-Wide Default to Private for accounts. Create permission sets for each marketing Team, and create an Inside Sales Team profile with the "View All" setting for accounts.

Set the Organization Wide Default to Private for accounts. Create criteria-based sharing rules for Each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team profile with the "View All" setting for Accounts.

sourceExplanation: Set the Organization-Wide Default (OWD) to Private for Accounts, create criteria-based sharing rules for each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team profile with the “View All” permission for Accounts is the correct solution because it satisfies all visibility requirements while following Salesforce security best practices. Private OWD ensures field sales reps can only see Accounts they own by default. Criteria-based sharing rules can be configured to share Accounts with the North American and European marketing teams based on region, ensuring each team only sees Accounts in their respective territories. Granting the Inside Sales team a profile with “View All” access allows them to see all Accounts, regardless of ownership or sharing rules. Why the other options are incorrect: OWD Public + profiles for marketing teams + Inside Sales role at top of hierarchy: Public OWD would allow all users to see all Accounts, which violates the requirement that field sales reps only see Accounts they own. OWD Public + criteria-based sharing rules + Inside Sales permission set with “View All”: Public OWD already grants visibility to all Accounts, making the sharing rules unnecessary and failing to restrict access for field sales reps. OWD Private + permission sets for marketing teams + Inside Sales profile with “View All”: Permission sets do not control record visibility by criteria. Without sharing rules, marketing teams would not be limited to Accounts in their specific regions.

stem: Sales reps at Universal Containers create multiple quotes per opportunity. Which automation tool should an app builder recommend to delete rejected quotes?
sourceExplanation: Flow is the correct automation tool because it can automatically take action on records when specific conditions are met. A record-triggered flow can detect when a Quote is marked as Rejected and then automatically delete that Quote. This allows Universal Containers to clean up rejected quotes without manual intervention. Why the other options are incorrect: Approval process: Approval processes are designed to manage record approvals and status changes. They cannot automatically delete records based on outcome without additional automation. Einstein Next Best Action: Einstein Next Best Action provides recommendations to users, not automated data actions such as deleting records. Validation rule: Validation rules only prevent invalid data entry; they cannot delete records.

stem: An app builder wants to create a custom Sync button on Account that will Call a Lightning Web Component that connects with an external system. This action Should only be available if the custom Status field is set to Ready to Syn What should an app builder use to add this functionality to an Account record page?
sourceExplanation: Dynamic action is the correct choice because it allows an app builder to add a custom button (Quick Action) to an Account record page that can conditionally appear based on field values. In this case, the Sync button can be configured to only display when the custom Status field equals “Ready to Sync” and can launch a Lightning Web Component (LWC) that connects to an external system. This provides both the required functionality and conditional visibility without custom code. Why the other options are incorrect: Custom link: Custom links can launch URLs but do not support conditional visibility based on record field values on Lightning record pages. Formula field: Formula fields are used to calculate and display values. They cannot create buttons or invoke Lightning Web Components. AppExchange product: An AppExchange product is not required to build native Salesforce functionality like a conditional Sync button tied to an LWC.

stem: Universal Containers uses a custom object called Projects. When managers Assign projects, they set a custom field on the Project record called Estimated Hours. Once set, users should be able to decrease but not increase the value. How can an app builder meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a validation rule that uses the ISCHANGED function.
Create a formula default value for the custom fiel
Create a validation rule that uses the PRIORVALUE function.
Create a formula field that uses the PREVGROUPVAL function.

sourceExplanation: Create a validation rule that uses the PRIORVALUE function is the correct solution because it allows Salesforce to compare the previous value of the Estimated Hours field with the new value being saved. The validation rule can prevent the save when the new value is greater than the prior value, while still allowing users to decrease the number. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a validation rule that uses the ISCHANGED function: ISCHANGED only detects whether a field has changed, not how it changed. It cannot determine whether the value increased or decreased. Create a formula default value for the custom field: A default value only applies when a record is created and does not control how the field can be edited later. Create a formula field that uses the PREVGROUPVAL function: PREVGROUPVAL is used in reports to compare values between grouped rows and cannot be used to enforce validation on record edits.

stem: What should an app builder consider when choosing a template for a new Lightning record page?

options.text: Page structure will automatically adapt to the device being used to view the record page.
To view the record page, users need "View All Data" permissions for the object.
The template is unable to be changed after the initial save.
Select a new template for each type of device users use to view the record page.

sourceExplanation: Page structure will automatically adapt to the device being used to view the record page is the correct consideration when choosing a Lightning record page template. Lightning App Builder templates are responsive, meaning the layout automatically adjusts for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices without requiring separate templates. Why the other options are incorrect: To view the record page, users need “View All Data” permissions for the object: Users only need appropriate object and record access. “View All Data” is an administrative permission and is not required to view record pages. The template is unable to be changed after the initial save: Lightning record page templates can be changed later by editing the page in Lightning App Builder. Select a new template for each type of device users use to view the record page: A single Lightning record page template works across all supported devices due to Salesforce’s responsive design.

stem: Dreamhouse Realty (DR) has many properties for sale and wants to identify the highest value of all offer records on each Property_record Which solution should the app builder use to meet DR's needs provided that there is a Master-detail relationship between the objects?
sourceExplanation: Roll-Up Summary is the correct solution because it can automatically calculate values from related child records when there is a Master-Detail relationship. In this case, a roll-up summary field on the Property (parent) record can be configured to calculate the MAX (highest value) of all related Offer records. This allows Dreamhouse Realty to easily identify the highest offer for each property without custom code. Why the other options are incorrect: Text Area (Long): A long text area field is used to store large amounts of text and cannot perform calculations or summarize related records. Multi-select Picklist: Multi-select picklists allow multiple values to be selected but cannot calculate or determine a highest value. Rich Text Area: Rich text area fields are used for formatted text and do not support numeric aggregation or roll-up calculations.

stem: An app builder needs to deploy a new account detail page layout from Sandbox to production. Which three components should an app builder include in the Change Set to ensure it Deploys successfully and visually as expected?
sourceExplanation: To deploy a new Account detail page layout from Sandbox to Production and ensure it appears correctly, the app builder should include the following components in the Change Set: Detail Page Layout – The layout itself defines the arrangement of fields, sections, and related lists on the Account record page. Custom Actions – Any custom actions (Quick Actions, Global Actions) used on the page must be included so they appear and function properly. Custom Fields – If the layout includes custom fields, they must be deployed; otherwise, the layout will break or not display as intended. Why the other options are incorrect: System Administrator profile: Profiles are only needed if you are deploying field-level security or page layout assignments. Including the profile is optional unless you need to preserve these settings. Lightning App Builder: The Lightning App Builder page is separate from the record page layout. If only the standard Account detail layout is being deployed, including the App Builder page is not necessary.

stem: Which three options are available when activating a Lightning page from The Lightning App Builder?

options.text: Assign the page to a combination of apps and permission sets.
Assign the page to a combination of apps and profiles.
Make the page the default homepage for specific apps.
Make the page the default homepage for specific roles.
Make the page the org default.

sourceExplanation: When activating a Lightning page from Lightning App Builder, an app builder can control where and for whom the page is available. The correct options are: Assign the page to a combination of apps and profiles – Lets you control page visibility based on the app and the user profiles. Make the page the default homepage for specific apps – Allows the page to appear as the homepage when users open a particular app. Make the page the org default – Sets the page as the default for all users across the organization unless overridden by app or profile assignments. Why the other options are incorrect: Assign the page to a combination of apps and permission sets: Lightning pages cannot be assigned to permission sets; assignments are based on apps and profiles only. Make the page the default homepage for specific roles: Activation does not support role-based default page assignment. Visibility is controlled through profiles and apps.

stem: To increase adoption, Universal Containers is proposing changes to its Salesforce data model to allow easier visibility for sales reps into key metrics. The Proposal has three custom objects related to the Account object, one with a master- Detail, and two that are not. Each of these objects has 15 fields they would like to Summarize on the Account object. What are two considerations for this proposal?

options.text: Roll-up summaries are limited to master-detail relationships.
Roll-up summaries allow MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT, and AVG.
An object can have 25 roll-up summaries.
An object can have 20 object references.

sourceExplanation: The correct considerations for this proposal are: Roll-up summaries are limited to master-detail relationships – Only objects in a master-detail relationship can use roll-up summary fields. The two custom objects that are not in a master-detail relationship cannot directly roll up their fields to the Account object. An object can have 25 roll-up summaries – Salesforce enforces a limit of 25 roll-up summary fields per object, so planning is needed when summarizing multiple fields (e.g., 15 fields from three objects might exceed limits). Why the other options are incorrect: Roll-up summaries allow MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT, and AVG: While this is true, it’s a capability, not a consideration or limitation impacting the proposal. An object can have 20 object references: This refers to the total number of lookup or master-detail relationships on an object, which is not directly relevant to summarizing fields on the Account.

stem: Universal Containers has a requirement that an opportunity should have a field ing the value of its associated account's billing state. This value should be static After the opportunity has been create What is the recommended solution to configure this automation behavior?
sourceExplanation: Flow is the correct solution because it can copy the Account’s Billing State to the Opportunity when the Opportunity is created and ensure the value remains static afterward. A record-triggered flow can be set to run only on create, populating a custom Opportunity field with the Account’s Billing State. Why the other options are incorrect: Apex: Apex could achieve this, but Salesforce declarative automation (Flow) can meet the requirement without custom code, which is preferred when possible. Roll-up summary field: Roll-up summaries only work for aggregating child records on a parent object. They cannot copy a parent field value to a child. Formula field: Formula fields are dynamic and always reflect the current value of the referenced field. They cannot store a static snapshot of the Account’s Billing State.

stem: Universal Containers has several new fields they've requested for the Opportunity Product object. What should an app builder be able to configure using a formula field?

options.text: A hyperlink to the parent Account of the parent Opportunity.
A Rich Text area field that uses HTML to bold certain characters.
A combination of the Opportunity's Text and a Description fields.
A mix of functions and concatenation of 10 Account fields and 10 Opportunity fields.

sourceExplanation: A Rich Text area field that uses HTML to bold certain characters is the correct option because formula fields on the Opportunity Product (or any object) can use Rich Text Area formulas with HTML tags to format text dynamically. This allows app builders to highlight or style text without creating additional fields or using code. Why the other options are incorrect: A hyperlink to the parent Account of the parent Opportunity: Formulas can create hyperlinks, but navigating two levels up (Opportunity → Account) is not directly supported in a formula field on the Opportunity Product. A combination of the Opportunity's Text and a Description fields: Formulas can concatenate fields, but the option implies only a basic concatenation, which is trivial and not the key capability being highlighted. A mix of functions and concatenation of 10 Account fields and 10 Opportunity fields: Formulas have a character and complexity limit, so combining 20 fields across multiple objects exceeds practical limits and is not recommended.

stem: DreamHouse Realty (DHR) recently acquired Cloud Kicks (CK), a company That is still on Salesforce Classi DHR is keeping the CK Salesforce org; however, it Will migrate this org to Lightning Experience. Where should the app builder find prebuilt resources to help with this project and Overall adoption?
sourceExplanation: AppExchange is the correct choice because it provides prebuilt resources, apps, and tools that can help with migrating from Salesforce Classic to Lightning Experience and improve user adoption. Organizations can find adoption dashboards, migration assistants, and Lightning-ready apps to streamline the transition. Why the other options are incorrect: Flow Builder: Flow Builder is used to automate business processes within Salesforce, not to provide prebuilt adoption or migration resources. Lightning Object Creator: This tool is used to quickly create objects from spreadsheets and does not provide resources for migration or adoption. Import Wizard: The Import Wizard is used to import data into Salesforce objects and is unrelated to migration guidance or adoption resources.

stem: Universal Containers uses a custom picklist field Account Region on the Account recor They want this region to be reflected on all related contact records And stay in sync if the value of this field changes on the Account. How should an app builder meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a picklist field called 'Account Region' on Contact object > Create a Lookup Relationship to Update this field if the Account Region field on the Account is change
Create a formula field on the Contact object > Set the value of the formula to ISPICKVAL (Account.Account_Region_o).
Create a text field called 'Account Region' on Contact object > Create a Lookup Relationship to Update this field if the Account Region field on the Account is change
Create a formula field on the Contact object > Set the value of the formula to TEXT (Account.Account Region_e).

sourceExplanation: Create a formula field on the Contact object and set the value to TEXT(Account.Account_Region__c) is the correct solution. This approach ensures that the Contact’s Account Region always reflects the current value from the parent Account. Formula fields are dynamic, so any changes on the Account automatically update on all related Contacts, keeping the data in sync without manual intervention. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a picklist field on Contact + Lookup relationship to update: Picklist fields on Contact cannot automatically stay in sync with the Account without custom automation like Flow or Apex. Create a formula field using ISPICKVAL: ISPICKVAL is used for conditional logic in formulas, not for simply displaying the picklist value on another object. Create a text field on Contact + Lookup relationship to update: A text field does not maintain a live link to the Account’s picklist value. Changes on the Account would not automatically reflect on the Contact without additional automation.

stem: DreamHouse Realty wants to track how many lifts are being installed into Customer garages. The To Be Installed custom checkbox field on the custom Lift Object should be checked and an external system should be notified via an outbound Message the next day when a lift is sold. Which automation tool should be used to complete this task?
sourceExplanation: Flow is the correct solution because a record-triggered flow can detect when a Lift is sold, update the To Be Installed checkbox, and then schedule an action to send an Outbound Message the next day. Flows allow both field updates and time-based actions, making it ideal for this scenario. Why the other options are incorrect: Approval process: Approval processes are designed to manage approvals and cannot automatically update fields or send scheduled outbound messages. Validation rule: Validation rules only enforce data integrity; they cannot update fields or trigger outbound messages. Assignment rule: Assignment rules are used for routing records like Leads or Cases and cannot perform field updates or send notifications.

stem: Cloud Kicks asked the app builder to insert a list of 25,000 records using Deduplication for the Delivery custom object. Which tool should be used?
sourceExplanation: Import Wizard is the correct tool because it is user-friendly, supports custom objects, and can handle up to 50,000 records. While it doesn’t offer advanced deduplication like Data Loader with external IDs, it provides built-in duplicate management by matching on standard or custom fields, making it suitable for Cloud Kicks’ Delivery records. Why the other options are incorrect: Data Loader: Data Loader is better for very large volumes of records or complex automations, but it does not provide built-in duplicate management during import; deduplication must be handled via external IDs or manual configuration. Lightning Object Creator: This tool is for creating objects quickly from spreadsheets, not importing or deduplicating large datasets. Schema Builder: Schema Builder is used to visualize and modify object structures. It cannot import or deduplicate records.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters has two custom objects that are part of a master- Detail relationship. What determines the ownership and sharing access of the detail record?

options.text: The owner is set independently on the detail object's settings.
The default owner is set in the parent object's settings.
The Owner field on the Detail record
The Owner field on the Master record

sourceExplanation: The Owner field on the Master record is the correct answer because in a master-detail relationship, the detail record automatically inherits the owner of the master record. Additionally, the sharing and access of the detail record are controlled by the master record, so the detail record does not have its own independent owner. Why the other options are incorrect: The owner is set independently on the detail object's settings: Detail records cannot have independent ownership in a master-detail relationship. The default owner is set in the parent object's settings: While the parent record may have a default owner, the key factor is that the detail inherits the actual owner of the master record, not a default setting. The Owner field on the Detail record: Detail records do not have their own Owner field in a master-detail relationship; ownership is inherited from the master.

stem: Universal Containers has a custom object that holds over 100 fields. The App builder wants to break up the fields into separate tabs on the lightning page. Which Lightning component is most appropriate to fulfil this requirement?
sourceExplanation: Accordion is the correct Lightning component because it allows the app builder to organize a large number of fields into collapsible sections on a Lightning record page. This improves usability and makes it easier for users to navigate over 100 fields without overwhelming the interface. Why the other options are incorrect: Highlights Panel: Displays key fields at the top of the page but does not allow grouping fields into multiple sections or tabs. Record Detail: Shows all fields in a single section; it does not support splitting fields across multiple tabs or collapsible sections. Field Section: Allows grouping of fields, but each section is static on the page. It does not provide collapsible functionality like the Accordion component, which is better suited for large numbers of fields.

stem: An app builder is tasked with adding key performance indicators on client Pages. They want to see a summary of the number of open Opportunities and the Number of won Opportunities for each Account. Where should the app builder go to build these new rollups?
sourceExplanation: Account Object is the correct place to build these roll-ups because roll-up summary fields are created on the master object in a master-detail relationship (or standard object in the case of Opportunities → Account). Here, the Account is the parent, and the roll-up summary fields can count related Opportunities that are open or won. Why the other options are incorrect: Lightning Object Creator: Used to quickly create objects from spreadsheets, not to build roll-up summary fields. Opportunity Object: Roll-up summary fields cannot be created on the child object; they must be on the parent (Account) to summarize related Opportunity data. Lightning App Builder: Used to design Lightning pages and add components, but roll-up summary fields are configured on the object itself, not in the page builder.

stem: Shipments at Cloud Kicks (CK) are created and updated by the warehouse staff in a Shipping application. The information needs to be pushed into Salesforce on a regular Basis. CK's app builder creates a custom object called Delivery_c to track the Information. How can the app builder prevent creating duplicate delivery records and update the Correct existing records when migrating data from the shipping application?

options.text: Use the Import Wizard and match on the tracking number.
Create a unique External ID field and use Dataloader.
Use the Import Wizard and match on the Salesforce I
Create a duplicate/match rule and use Dataloader.

sourceExplanation: Create a unique External ID field and use Data Loader is the correct solution. By defining an External ID on the Delivery__c object (e.g., tracking number or shipment ID), the app builder can use Data Loader to upsert records. This approach ensures that: Existing records are updated if the External ID matches. Duplicates are not created for the same delivery. Upserting with an External ID is the standard Salesforce approach for syncing data from external systems. Why the other options are incorrect: Use the Import Wizard and match on the tracking number: The Import Wizard has limited deduplication capabilities and does not allow upsert based on custom external IDs, making it less reliable for preventing duplicates in large datasets. Use the Import Wizard and match on the Salesforce ID: Matching on Salesforce IDs requires knowing the internal IDs in advance, which is not practical for syncing external system data. Create a duplicate/match rule and use Data Loader: Duplicate rules help prevent duplicates but do not automatically update existing records. Upsert via an External ID is required to update records reliably.

stem: Dreamhouse Realty requires that field value changes for certain fields such As Asking Price_c and Real Estate Agent on their House_c custom object up prominently on Chatter. Which Chatter feature should the app builder use?
sourceExplanation: Feed Tracking is the correct Chatter feature because it allows Salesforce to track changes to specified fields on an object and post updates to the Chatter feed. By enabling feed tracking on the House__c object for fields like Asking_Price__c and Real_Estate_Agent__c, users will see changes prominently in the feed, improving visibility and collaboration. Why the other options are incorrect: Topics: Used to categorize and tag records or posts for search and organization, not to track field changes. Pin Field: Pins a field to the highlights panel on a record page; it does not post updates to Chatter. Publisher Actions: Allow users to post updates or create records from the Chatter feed, but do not automatically track field changes.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters uses a custom object to track travel requests. Rangers want to have automatic posts on a record whenever a travel request has been approving Which feature should be used to accomplish this?
sourceExplanation: Feed Tracking is the correct feature because it allows automatic posts to Chatter whenever specified fields on a record change. By enabling feed tracking on the Travel Request custom object for fields like Approval Status, Salesforce will automatically post updates to the record feed whenever a travel request is approved, keeping Rangers informed in real time. Why the other options are incorrect: Auto-response rule: Sends email notifications when records are created or updated, but does not post to Chatter. Approval process: Manages approval routing and actions but does not automatically create Chatter posts unless combined with feed tracking or custom actions. Feed quick action: Allows users to manually post to Chatter from the feed but does not automate posts based on record changes.

stem: Universal Containers uses a custom object called Reviews to capture Information generated by interviewers during the candidate process. The Review records are visible to any user that has access to the related custom Candidate record The VP of Human Resources wants the comment field on the Review to be private to anyone outside of the HR department. How should the app builder meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a page layout with the field and use field-level security to hide the field from all other users.
Create a sharing rule to share the field with the VP of HR with Role and Subordinates.
Create a page layout with the field for HR users and another page layout without the field for all other users.
Create an Apex sharing rule to share the field with users that have "HR" in their role.

sourceExplanation: Create a page layout with the field and use field-level security to hide the field from all other users is the correct solution. By configuring field-level security, the app builder can ensure that the Comment field on the Review object is only visible to HR users while remaining hidden from everyone else who has access to the related Candidate record. This approach enforces privacy at the field level without requiring code. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a sharing rule to share the field with the VP of HR with Role and Subordinates: Sharing rules control record-level access, not field-level access. They cannot make a specific field private. Create a page layout with the field for HR users and another page layout without the field for all other users: While page layouts control visibility on the UI, field-level security is the proper way to enforce field privacy across all interfaces, including API access. Create an Apex sharing rule to share the field with users that have "HR" in their role: Apex sharing rules also only affect record-level access, not individual field access.

stem: Service agents at Ursa Major Solar want a more condensed case view. Service agents also want to be able to modify the associated contact and account Records from the case page layout on the Lightning record page. Which two components should an app builder use to meet these requirements?
sourceExplanation: To meet the requirements, the app builder should use the following components on the Case Lightning record page: Tabs – Allows the app builder to condense multiple sections (e.g., Details, Related Lists, Activities) into a compact, organized layout. This helps service agents navigate information efficiently. Related Record – Displays fields from related objects, such as Contact and Account, directly on the case page and allows inline editing, so agents can modify related records without leaving the page. Why the other options are incorrect: Path: Used to visually guide users through stages (like case status) but does not condense page layout sections or allow editing of related records. Rich Text: Displays static text, instructions, or formatting on the page but cannot provide editable fields or condense sections for better usability.

stem: Sales reps want the ability to see who can view their account records and How the people have access. Which button should the app builder add to the Account page layout to enable this?
sourceExplanation: Sharing is the correct button because it lets sales reps see who has access to a specific account record and why—whether through manual sharing, sharing rules, or role hierarchy. When added to the Account page layout, clicking this button opens the Sharing Detail for the record, providing transparency into record-level access. Why the other options are incorrect: Sharing Hierarchy: Shows users higher in the role hierarchy and their access, but does not show detailed sharing for that specific record. New Task / Edit: Used for creating tasks or modifying the record itself; they do not provide information about record access.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to start tracking how many shoe subscriptions have been Sold for each shoe catalog. A master-detail relationship exists between the Subscription And the shoe_c objects. Which type of field should an app builder create?
sourceExplanation: Roll-up summary field is the correct solution because it allows the app builder to aggregate data from child records (Subscription) on the parent record (Shoe__c). Since a master-detail relationship exists, a roll-up summary can calculate the count of subscriptions sold for each shoe catalog automatically. Why the other options are incorrect: Lookup field: Creates a relationship between objects but does not perform aggregation or counting. Master-detail field: Defines the relationship but does not itself summarize child records. Sum field: There is no standard "Sum" field type in Salesforce; roll-up summary fields are used to calculate sums, counts, or other aggregates in master-detail relationships.

stem: Sales reps at Universal Containers use Salesforce on their mobile devices. They want a way to add new contacts quickly and then follow up later to complete the Additional information necessary. Which mobile solution should an app builder recommend to create the new contact?

options.text: A Build a global action to create Contacts.
Use Path and set pre-defined values.
Customize the mobile menu to move Contacts to the top.
Add a compact layout to Contacts.

sourceExplanation: Build a global action to create Contacts is the correct solution because global actions allow users to quickly create records from anywhere in the Salesforce mobile app. By setting predefined or minimal fields, sales reps can add new contacts rapidly and then follow up later to complete additional information. Why the other options are incorrect: Use Path and set pre-defined values: Paths guide users through stages of a process (e.g., Opportunity stages) but do not provide a quick way to create new records. Customize the mobile menu to move Contacts to the top: This only makes the Contacts tab more accessible but does not streamline record creation. Add a compact layout to Contacts: Compact layouts control which fields appear in highlights or previews but do not provide a way to create new records quickly.

stem: Ursa Major Solar (UMS) is planning to hire some new employees. UMS Wants to allow a job candidate (Job Candidate_c) to apply for multiple open Positions (Open_Position__c) and then be able to view the applications (Application_c) on the job candidate's recor UMS also wants to view all the Applications for a specific open position. What should an app builder recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a master-detail relationship field on Application__c to Open_Position__c
Create a master-detail relationship field on Application__c to Job Candidate
Create a master detail relationship on Open_Position__c to Application__c
Create a master-detail relationship field on Job candidate to Application_c.

sourceExplanation: To meet the requirements, the app builder should create two master-detail relationships on the Application__c object: Master-detail relationship to Job_Candidate__c – This links each application to the candidate, allowing the candidate record to display all related applications. Master-detail relationship to Open_Position__c – This links each application to the open position, allowing the position record to display all related applications. This configuration creates a junction object (Application__c) between Job_Candidate__c and Open_Position__c, enabling a many-to-many relationship where candidates can apply for multiple positions and positions can have multiple candidates. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a master-detail on Application__c to only Open_Position__c: This allows viewing applications from the position side but does not relate applications back to the candidate. Create a master-detail on Open_Position__c to Application__c: The master object in a master-detail relationship should be the parent; this setup does not model candidates applying to multiple positions properly. Create a master-detail on Job_Candidate__c to Application__c: Same issue: only models one side of the relationship and does not support many-to-many applications.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) needs a picklist field called Status on three Separate custom objects. UC has a requirement to share the list of values for this field Across each object. Which feature should an app builder use?
sourceExplanation: Global Picklist Value Set is the correct feature because it allows an app builder to define a single set of picklist values and reuse it across multiple objects. By creating a global picklist for Status, the same list of values can be applied to all three custom objects, ensuring consistency and easier maintenance. Why the other options are incorrect: Shared Custom Field: There is no standard Salesforce feature called “Shared Custom Field” for sharing picklist values across objects. Dependent Picklist: Dependent picklists control visibility of one picklist based on the value of another, not sharing values across objects. Related Picklist: Related picklists do not exist as a standard Salesforce feature; this is not a valid option for sharing picklist values.

stem: When a sales rep submits an account for approval, Universal Containers Wants the user to answer additional questions via a popup window to populate Additional record fields. What should an app builder use to achieve the desired result?
sourceExplanation: Custom button and Flow is the correct solution because a custom button can launch a screen flow when the user submits an account for approval. The screen flow can display a popup window with fields and questions that the user must complete, and then update additional fields on the Account record. This approach is declarative, avoids code, and meets the requirement for capturing extra information during submission. Why the other options are incorrect: Custom object: Creating a new object does not address the need for a popup or collecting additional information during approval. Visualforce page: Requires coding and is unnecessary when a declarative solution with Flow can achieve the same functionality. Custom Lightning component: Could work, but using a Flow with a button is simpler, faster to implement, and fully declarative.

stem: The finance manager at Universal Containers wants to receive a new Business notification email each time a new client is won. The sales manager wants to Receive a task letting them know to onboard the new client unless it is a top-tier Client. Which automation tool should an app builder use to best address all these requests?
sourceExplanation: Record-triggered Flow is the correct solution because it can automatically execute multiple actions when a record is created or updated. In this case: Send an email notification to the finance manager when a client is won. Create a task for the sales manager to onboard the client, with a condition to exclude top-tier clients. Flows allow declarative, conditional automation without code, meeting both requirements in a single process. Why the other options are incorrect: Approval process: Designed for routing records for approval; it cannot send conditional onboarding tasks based on client tier. Apex: Could achieve the requirements but requires coding; a declarative Flow is preferred. Screen flow: Requires user interaction and cannot run automatically on record creation or update.

stem: Universal Containers wants to dynamically display a component on a Lightning record page for an account based on criteria about the related contact. Which solution should an app builder use to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Add a related record component to the page layout.
Hide the component behind a tab on the page layout.
Set the filter type on the component visibility to display based on user permissions, using custom Permission to define the dynamic criteria
Set the component visibility to display based on an advanced filter type, using the contact field(s) to Define the dynamic criteria

sourceExplanation: Set the component visibility to display based on an advanced filter type, using the contact field(s) to define the dynamic criteria is the correct solution. Lightning App Builder allows components on a record page to be conditionally displayed using advanced filters that reference fields on related records. This approach dynamically shows or hides the component based on the criteria defined for the related Contact. Why the other options are incorrect: Add a related record component to the page layout: Displays related record information but does not provide dynamic visibility based on field criteria. Hide the component behind a tab on the page layout: Tabs only organize content; they do not dynamically show or hide components based on data. Set the filter type on the component visibility to display based on user permissions: Filters based on user permissions cannot evaluate related record fields; this would not meet the requirement for dynamic visibility based on Contact criteria.

stem: Universal Containers wants to embed a chart of all related Opportunities, By stage, on the Account detail page. Which type of report should an app builder create to add to the Account page layout?

options.text: A tabular report on the Opportunity object
A tabular report on the Account object
A summary report on the Opportunity object
A summary report on the Account object

sourceExplanation: A summary report on the Opportunity object is the correct choice because summary reports allow grouping of records by fields such as Opportunity Stage. By creating this report and grouping by Stage, the app builder can generate a chart and embed it on the Account record page to show all related Opportunities by stage. Why the other options are incorrect: A tabular report on the Opportunity object: Tabular reports list records but do not support grouping, which is required to summarize by stage for charting. A tabular report on the Account object: Accounts cannot summarize related Opportunities; tabular format does not allow grouping or charting. A summary report on the Account object: Grouping Accounts does not summarize their related Opportunities; the report must be on the Opportunity object to show stage breakdown.

stem: An app builder has created a new report type but users are unable to select it from the Report Type list when making a new report for records they own. What could be causing this issue?

options.text: The report type is in a status of In Development.
Access to the necessary object is unavailable.
The report type is in a status of Deploye
Access to Create and Customize Reports is disable

sourceExplanation: The report type is in a status of In Development is the correct answer. Custom report types must be deployed before users can select them when creating reports. If a report type is still In Development, it is only visible to the app builder and cannot be used by other users. Why the other options are incorrect: Access to the necessary object is unavailable: While object-level permissions affect data visibility, the report type would still appear in the list; users just wouldn’t see data. The report type is in a status of Deployed: Deployed report types are fully available; this status does not prevent users from selecting them. Access to Create and Customize Reports is disabled: If this permission were disabled, users couldn’t create any reports at all, not just be unable to see a specific report type.

stem: The appraisal team at DreamHouse Realty wants to leverage Salesforce Mobile app. What are three things an app builder should do to optimize mobile experience?

options.text: Avoid using default field values so that the user is required to fill in all fields on the screen.
Minimize the amount of formula fields and lookup fields to reduce page load time.
Put the most important fields in the compact layout so they are easy to fin
Create individual customized layouts for different phone operating systems.
Use Global Actions to make it easy to perform vital functionality on mobile.

sourceExplanation: To optimize the Salesforce Mobile app experience for the appraisal team, an app builder should focus on performance, usability, and accessibility: Minimize the amount of formula fields and lookup fields – Reduces page load times on mobile devices and improves responsiveness. Put the most important fields in the compact layout – Ensures key information is easily visible at the top of the record on mobile screens. Use Global Actions – Provides quick access to vital functionality, such as creating records or logging calls, directly from the mobile app. Why the other option is incorrect: Avoid using default field values: Default field values can actually improve efficiency on mobile by reducing the number of fields users need to fill in, so avoiding them is not necessarily beneficial. Create individual customized layouts for different phone operating systems: Salesforce mobile layouts are cross-platform; creating separate layouts per OS is unnecessary and does not optimize the mobile experience.

stem: Universal Containers wants to create a custom checkbox formula field on The Opportunity object. This formula should evaluate to true if the following conditions Are met: Stage is set to Negotiation/Review, Close Date is less than 1 week away. Which formula meets these requirements?
sourceExplanation: The correct formula is AND(ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Negotiation/Review"), CloseDate -TODAY() <= 7) because: ISPICKVAL correctly checks the picklist value "Negotiation/Review". CloseDate - TODAY() calculates the days until close date. <= 7 ensures it's within a week (including today). Why the other options are incorrect: A: Incorrect syntax and DAY(7) function usage. B: CloseDate – 7 < TODAY() checks if close date is more than 7 days ago, not less than 1 week away. C: Incorrect picklist comparison syntax (should use ISPICKVAL or TEXT).

stem: An app builder has downloaded a component from the AppExchange Successfully; however, they are unable to add it to the Lightning home page. Which two reasons can be preventing the app builder from being able to add the Custom component?

options.text: A custom tab must be created to add custom components to the page with the App Builder.
The component requires a developer permission to add it to the page with the App Builder.
My Domain must be deployed to add custom components to the page with the App Builder.
The component is tagged for record pages instead of home pages and is not ing up in The App Builder.

sourceExplanation: The two correct reasons are: My Domain must be deployed to add custom components to the page with the App Builder: Salesforce requires My Domain to be deployed before custom Lightning components can be added to pages. Without it, the component will not appear in the Lightning App Builder. The component is tagged for record pages instead of home pages and is not showing up in the App Builder: Components are configured with page type availability. If a component is only available for record pages, it cannot be added to a home page. Why the other options are incorrect: A custom tab must be created to add custom components to the page with the App Builder: Custom tabs are not required to add a component to a Lightning page; this does not prevent the component from appearing. The component requires a developer permission to add it to the page with the App Builder: While some components may have licensing or access requirements, standard installation from AppExchange does not require a developer permission to add the component if it is available and My Domain is deployed.

stem: Universal Containers utilizes opportunities and a custom object called Detailed_Sales_c The company would like to roll sales metrics up to an opportunity For only Detailed_Sales_c records that have their picklist status set to Active. What is the recommended method for the app builder to achieve this request?

options.text: Utilize the AppExchange to download a third-party application that can roll up the sales dollars with The appropriate filter.
Utilize Apex code to roll up the desired amounts.
Create a master detail relationship between the parent and child object with a roll up summary field That filters on the status field
Create a lookup relationship between the parent and child object with a roll-up summary field that Filters on the status field

sourceExplanation: Create a master-detail relationship between the parent and child object with a roll-up summary field that filters on the Status field is the correct solution. Roll-up summary fields in Salesforce only work on master-detail relationships and can be configured to aggregate child records based on criteria, such as the picklist Status = Active. This declarative approach meets the requirement without writing code or using third-party apps. Why the other options are incorrect: Utilize the AppExchange to download a third-party application: While possible, this adds unnecessary complexity when Salesforce can handle filtered roll-ups natively via master-detail relationships. Utilize Apex code: Custom code is not required because Salesforce roll-up summary fields already support filtered aggregation. Create a lookup relationship between the parent and child object with a roll-up summary field: Roll-up summary fields cannot be created on lookup relationships; they only work on master-detail relationships.

stem: At Cloud Kicks when an opportunity close date is delayed by more than 60 days, the Manager and the VP of Sales want to review the change. Which two solutions will meet the requirement?

options.text: Build an approval process that requires unanimous approval from the manager and VP of Sales.
Build a validation rule that does not allow a user to save the opportunity recor
Create a formula field that calculates if the close date is less than 60 days and then send An email alert.
Create a flow that submits the record for an approval process.

sourceExplanation: The two correct solutions are: Build an approval process that requires unanimous approval from the manager and VP of Sales: This ensures that when an Opportunity’s Close Date is delayed, the record must be reviewed and approved by both the manager and VP before changes are finalized. Create a flow that submits the record for an approval process: A record-triggered or scheduled flow can automatically detect when the Close Date changes by more than 60 days and submit the Opportunity for approval, ensuring timely review without relying on manual submission. Why the other options are incorrect: Build a validation rule that does not allow a user to save the opportunity record: Validation rules prevent saving data entirely; they cannot route records for review or handle approval workflows. Create a formula field that calculates if the close date is less than 60 days and then send an email alert: Formula fields cannot trigger actions like sending email alerts. A workflow, process builder, or flow is required to send notifications.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) delivers purchased containers to remote Construction sites. Customers supply UC with crossroads or location markers. Which field type should the app builder use to capture this information?
sourceExplanation: Geolocation is the correct field type because it allows users to capture latitude and longitude coordinates for specific locations. This is ideal for UC to track crossroads or location markers for delivery sites, enabling location-based features such as distance calculations or mapping. Why the other options are incorrect: Number: A number field cannot store both latitude and longitude or support geolocation calculations. Reference: Reference fields link to another record but do not capture geographic coordinates. External Lookup: Used to relate Salesforce records to external objects, not for storing location data.

stem: The CFO of Cloud Kicks needs a way for new vendors to accept terms on Agreements for any new major retail store lease before the opportunity can be close Which feature should be used to handle this requirement?
sourceExplanation: Approval Process is the correct feature because it can require new vendors to accept terms on Agreements before an Opportunity can be closed. By setting up an approval process with the Opportunity as the target object, the record can be locked until the necessary approvals or confirmations are completed, ensuring compliance before the deal is finalized. Why the other options are incorrect: Email Alert: Can notify users but cannot enforce acceptance or prevent closing an Opportunity. Dynamic Action: Controls visibility or availability of actions on the page but cannot enforce record-level approval requirements. Validation Rule: Can prevent saving a record based on conditions, but it cannot route records for approval or manage multi-step acceptance processes.

stem: An app builder is preparing to deploy a new app from the sandbox to Production using change sets. Which two considerations should an app builder keep in mind during this process?

options.text: Transactions will revert if the deployment errors.
Users should be logged out of production when receiving inbound change sets.
Salesforce Connect automatically establishes a link between environments.
Change sets do not include all components and may have to perform some changes. Manually

sourceExplanation: The two correct considerations are: Transactions will revert if the deployment errors: Change sets deploy components transactionally. If an error occurs during deployment, all changes in the change set are rolled back, leaving the org unchanged. Change sets do not include all components and may require some changes manually: Some metadata components (e.g., standard picklist values, certain settings) are not included in change sets. The app builder may need to manually configure or adjust these components after deployment. Why the other options are incorrect: Users should be logged out of production when receiving inbound change sets: Not required; users can remain logged in. Change set deployments do not require downtime. Salesforce Connect automatically establishes a link between environments: Salesforce Connect is unrelated to change sets and does not automatically link sandbox and production environments.

stem: At Ursa Major Solar there is a requirement for a new field called Planet Details on the Planet object where users can write detailed descriptions that can Include pictures and links. Which field type should the app builder utilize to fulfill this requirement?
sourceExplanation: Rich Text Area is the correct field type because it allows users to enter detailed descriptions with formatted text, images, and links. This meets the requirement for the Planet Details field, providing flexibility for rich content input directly on the Planet object. Why the other options are incorrect: Lightning Web Component: Components are used to create custom UI functionality, not to store field-level text data. URL: Only stores a single web address; it cannot contain formatted text or images. Long Text Area: Stores multiple lines of text but does not support rich formatting, images, or clickable links.

stem: Universal Containers wants to track installation information once a Container has been purchased on a custom object. Sales reps should have visibility of All the installations associated with their opportunities. Which kind of relationship should this new object have to Opportunity?
sourceExplanation: Master-Detail is the correct relationship type because it allows the custom Installation object to be a child of the Opportunity, giving sales reps visibility into all related installations. Master-detail relationships also enable features such as roll-up summary fields and inherited sharing settings, ensuring that users with access to the Opportunity can see associated installations automatically. Why the other options are incorrect: Hierarchical: Only available for the User object and cannot be used for custom objects. Many-to-Many: Requires a junction object; not necessary here because each installation is directly associated with a single Opportunity. Lookup: Lookup relationships allow optional associations and do not automatically inherit sharing and visibility from the parent Opportunity.

stem: What is the process to upgrade an unmanaged package that is currently installed in production?

options.text: Uninstall the current version and install the new version.
Use the Install Wizard to install the upgrade to production.
Install the new version to a Developer org then deploy to production.
Click the update link on the Installed Packages page.

sourceExplanation: Uninstall the current version and install the new version is the correct process for upgrading an unmanaged package. Unmanaged packages do not support direct upgrades; to move to a new version, you must remove the existing package from production and then install the updated version. Why the other options are incorrect: Use the Install Wizard to install the upgrade to production: The Install Wizard installs a package but cannot directly upgrade an unmanaged package without first uninstalling the existing version. Install the new version to a Developer org then deploy to production: This does not upgrade the package in production; unmanaged packages must be uninstalled and reinstalled. Click the update link on the Installed Packages page: Unmanaged packages do not have an update link; only managed packages support upgrades via the update link.

stem: Duplicate management for Leads has been implemented at Universal Containers but it seems duplicate leads are still being create The Org Wide Default (OWD) is set to "Private" for Leads. Which two actions help prevent duplicate Leads from being created?

options.text: Change the Lead Duplicate Rule details to Bypass Sharing Rules.
Change the Load Assignment Rule to check for duplicates.
Change OWD for Leads to Public Rea
Change the Lead Duplicate actions to Block on Create.

sourceExplanation: The two correct actions are: Change the Lead Duplicate Rule details to Bypass Sharing Rules: When OWD is set to Private, duplicate rules respect sharing settings by default. Enabling Bypass Sharing Rules ensures the duplicate rule can see all leads in the org and prevent duplicates, even if the user doesn’t have access to certain records. Change the Lead Duplicate actions to Block on Create: Setting the duplicate rule action to Block prevents users from saving a lead that matches an existing record, enforcing duplicate prevention at creation time. Why the other options are incorrect: Change the Lead Assignment Rule to check for duplicates: Assignment rules route leads but do not enforce duplicate prevention. Change OWD for Leads to Public Read/Write: Making OWD public is not required; duplicate rules can still function properly by bypassing sharing rules without changing overall access.

stem: The Recruiting team at AW Computing captures the job acceptance and date of hire of a candidate on the Job Application custom object. Once the candidate accepts the recruiter's Job offer, the date of hire should be entered and not be changed on subsequent record edits. Which validation formula should the app builder use?
sourceExplanation: NOT(ISBLANK(Job_Accepted__c)) && ISCHANGED(Hire_Date__c) is the correct formula. This formula enforces that: If the Job Accepted checkbox (Job_Accepted__c) is checked (not blank), Then the Hire Date (Hire_Date__c) cannot be changed. If a user tries to edit the Hire Date after the job is accepted, the validation rule evaluates to TRUE and prevents the save. Why the other options are incorrect: (ISBLANK(Job_Accepted__c) || NOT(ISCHANGED(Hire_Date__c)): Allows edits to the Hire Date even after Job Accepted is checked; does not enforce the restriction. (ISBLANK(Job_Accepted__c) && NOT(ISCHANGED(Hire_Date__c)): Only triggers when Job Accepted is blank and Hire Date is not changed; it does not prevent edits after acceptance. NOT(ISBLANK(Job_Accepted__c)) || ISCHANGED(Hire_Date__c): Uses OR logic, which would block edits unnecessarily or allow unwanted changes; it does not correctly enforce the rule.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) tracks the support level of its customers on the account Record page. CK wants to a text notification on a case record page when the Related account is a platinum-level customer. How can an app builder meet this requirement?

options.text: Clone the Case Lightning page. Add a rich text component to the new page, and assign this page to platinum accounts.
Add a rich text component to the Case Lighting page Set the component visibility of the rich text component to when the account support level is Platinum.
Create a text-only custom Lightning Web Component Drag the custom Lightning Web Component into the Case page layout.

Set its visibility to when the account support level is platinum. Create a text-only custom Lightning Web Component. Clone the case page layout. Drag the custom Lightning Web Component into the page, and assign the layout to platinum cases.

sourceExplanation: The correct solution is: Add a rich text component to the Case Lightning page. Set the component visibility of the rich text component to display only when the related Account’s Support Level is Platinum. This approach allows: Displaying a text notification dynamically on the Case record page. Using component visibility filters in Lightning App Builder to show the notification only for platinum-level accounts. Avoiding the need to create multiple page layouts or custom components. Why the other options are incorrect: Clone the Case Lightning page and assign the page to platinum accounts: Requires multiple page layouts and increases maintenance; unnecessary when component visibility can handle this declaratively. Create a text-only custom Lightning Web Component and drag it into the page: While possible, using a standard rich text component with visibility filters achieves the same goal without custom development. Clone the case page layout and assign it to platinum cases: Page layouts cannot be assigned dynamically based on related Account fields; they are assigned by profile or record type only.

stem: AW Computing uses a private sharing model for opportunities. Whenever An opportunity with a type of Service Agreement is created, all users in the Service Manager role should be able to view the opportunity. Which tool should AW Computing use to accomplish this?
sourceExplanation: Criteria-based sharing rules is the correct solution. Since AW Computing wants to share Opportunities with Type = Service Agreement to all users in the Service Manager role, a criteria-based sharing rule can be configured to: Automatically share records that meet specific criteria (Opportunity Type = Service Agreement). Grant access to a role, role and subordinates, or public group. This declarative solution works well with a private sharing model. Why the other options are incorrect: Owner-based sharing rules: Share records based on the owner; not suitable here because the sharing depends on the Opportunity Type, not the owner. Apex sharing rules: Allow programmatic sharing but are unnecessary because this can be accomplished declaratively with a criteria-based sharing rule. Manual sharing: Requires users to share records manually, which is not scalable or automated.

stem: An app builder at Ursa Major Solar has been working on a new custom app In a sandbox that has been upgraded to the next major Salesforce version, and their Production Instance is still on the current Salesforce version. The development is Complete and they are ready to deploy a change set. What should the app builder consider when planning the deployment?

options.text: The change set will be automatically deployed when production is upgrade
The deployment is not possible due to different versions.
The change set components will be upgraded to the next version in production.
It will fail if there is a feature only available in the next version.

sourceExplanation: It will fail if there is a feature only available in the next version is the correct consideration. When deploying a change set from a sandbox on a newer Salesforce version to a production org on an older version, any components that rely on features introduced in the newer version may fail to deploy. App builders should: Review all components for version-specific features. Test compatibility or remove unsupported features before deployment. Why the other options are incorrect: The change set will be automatically deployed when production is upgraded: Change sets do not automatically deploy; manual deployment is always required. The deployment is not possible due to different versions: Deployment is possible, but version-specific features may cause failures. The change set components will be upgraded to the next version in production: Components do not automatically upgrade; the sandbox and production maintain separate versioning until production itself is upgraded.

stem: An app builder needs to change the data type of some custom fields. Which two limitations should the app builder be aware of when changing the data Type of a custom field?

options.text: It is not possible to change the data type of a formula field to any data type.
It is not possible to change the data type of field referenced by Apex code.
It is not possible to change the data type of a field used as an External ID from number to Text.
It is not possible to change the data type of a Text Area (Long) field to Text.

sourceExplanation: The two correct limitations are: It is not possible to change the data type of a formula field to any data type: Formula fields are calculated fields; their data type is determined by the formula and cannot be changed to another type directly. It is not possible to change the data type of a field referenced by Apex code: Fields referenced in Apex classes or triggers cannot have their data type changed without first modifying or removing the dependent code, otherwise deployment or editing will fail. Why the other options are incorrect: It is not possible to change the data type of a field used as an External ID from number to Text: Some data type changes are allowed for fields used as External IDs; Salesforce may allow certain conversions after removing the External ID property temporarily. It is not possible to change the data type of a Text Area (Long) field to Text: Text Area (Long) fields have restrictions, but in some cases they can be converted to Text depending on field length; this is not a universal limitation.

stem: DreamHouse Realty wants to display a weather map component on a Lightning record page when a house is scheduled for a ing. How should the app builder meet the requirement?
sourceExplanation: Component visibility is the correct solution. In Lightning App Builder, you can configure visibility filters so that a component is displayed only when specific conditions are met—such as when a House record is scheduled for a showing. This allows the weather map component to appear dynamically without needing separate page layouts or custom code. Why the other options are incorrect: Field-level security: Controls who can see or edit field data, not whether a component appears on a page. Formula field: Can calculate values for display or logic but does not control component visibility on a Lightning page. Sharing rules: Determine record-level access, not whether a component is shown on a page.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) has several picklist fields on the Account object Whose values are routinely modified to meet changing business requirements. Due to These revolving changes, UC has a high number of inactive picklist values that are Impacting system performance and user experience. What can the app builder do to alleviate this issue?

options.text: Establish upper bound on existing picklists in Picklist Settings.
Set up Global Values in Picklist Value Sets.
Remove upper bound on inactive picklist values in Picklist Settings.
Convert the picklist fields to a different field type that will still meet the business requirements.

sourceExplanation: Set up Global Values in Picklist Value Sets is the correct solution. By using Global Picklist Value Sets, the app builder can: Maintain a centralized list of values that can be reused across multiple picklist fields. Reduce the number of inactive values in individual picklists, improving performance and user experience. Make updates easier since changes to the global value set automatically propagate to all fields using it. Why the other options are incorrect: Establish upper bound on existing picklists in Picklist Settings: This only limits the number of picklist entries but does not address reuse or central management of values. Remove upper bound on inactive picklist values in Picklist Settings: Increasing the limit does not reduce inactive values or improve performance; it may worsen it. Convert the picklist fields to a different field type: Changing the field type is disruptive and unnecessary; using global value sets resolves the issue declaratively.

stem: How should an app builder configure access to a contact's Twitter profile for Salesforce mobile app users?

options.text: Add a Twitter Quick Action to the mobile navigation.
Add an AppExchange Lightning Component to the mobile app.
Add the Twitter component to mobile view Lightning pages.
Add a formula field to the Contact page layout.

sourceExplanation: Add the Twitter component to mobile view Lightning pages is the correct solution. Salesforce provides a Social Customer Service / Social Accounts & Contacts integration that allows Twitter profiles to be displayed on Contact records. By placing the Twitter component on the Contact Lightning page and ensuring it is visible in the mobile view, mobile users can access the contact’s Twitter profile directly from the Salesforce mobile app. Why the other options are incorrect: Add a Twitter Quick Action to the mobile navigation: Quick Actions are for creating or updating records, not for displaying external social profiles. Add an AppExchange Lightning Component to the mobile app: Not required if the standard Twitter component is available; third-party components are unnecessary. Add a formula field to the Contact page layout: Formula fields can store URLs or text but cannot embed interactive Twitter profiles in the mobile app.

stem: A business user at Universal Containers wants to update an Account directly From an Opportunity recor What should the app builder create to allow the business user to make these edits?

options.text: Opportunity fields updated by a process.
Formula fields displaying the Account fields.
An update record action with a related record component.
An update record action with a detail's component.

sourceExplanation: An update record action with a related record component is the correct solution. In Lightning, a Related Record component can be placed on the Opportunity page to show fields from the related Account. By combining it with an Update Record quick action, users can edit Account fields directly from the Opportunity record page without navigating away, making data updates faster and more convenient. Why the other options are incorrect: Opportunity fields updated by a process: Processes can automate updates but do not allow direct, on-page editing by the user. Formula fields displaying the Account fields: Formula fields are read-only and cannot be edited by users. An update record action with a detail's component: The Detail component shows the current record’s fields (Opportunity) but does not allow editing fields of a related record like the Account.

stem: Cloud Kicks works on an annual subscription model. When a sales rep marks An opportunity as closed won, a new opportunity should automatically be created for The renewal. The contracts team works outside of Salesforce but also needs to be Notified about closed deals in order to initiate the contract process with the customer. Which automation solution would meet these requirements?
sourceExplanation: Record-triggered Flow is the correct solution because it can handle multiple actions automatically when an Opportunity is marked Closed Won: Create a new Opportunity for the renewal automatically. Send a notification (e.g., email alert or outbound message) to the contracts team so they can initiate the contract process. A flow allows declarative, automated, and conditional actions without requiring code. Why the other options are incorrect: Approval Process: Used to route records for approval; it cannot automatically create related opportunities or notify external teams. Outbound Message: Can notify external systems but cannot create a new opportunity. Validation Rule: Prevents invalid data entry but does not perform automation or notifications.

stem: The sales team receives a list of approximately 800 leads each morning from The marketing team. The marketing team does not know if any of the leads are Currently in the pipeline and sends the entire list each morning. Which tool should be used to import these leads into Salesforce while preventing the Duplicates from being inserted?
sourceExplanation: Data Import Wizard is the correct solution because it: Supports bulk import of leads (up to 50,000 records at a time). Can check for duplicates based on standard or custom matching rules during import. Is user-friendly and ideal for non-technical users like the marketing team. Why the other options are incorrect: Dataloader.io: While it can import records, duplicate management is not automatic unless configured; requires additional setup. Data Loader: Handles large volumes of data but does not automatically enforce Salesforce duplicate rules during import. Manual entry: Not practical for 800 leads daily; prone to errors and duplicates.

stem: The Director of Marketing at Northern Trail Outfitters wants the app builder to create a Formula field that tracks how many days have elapsed since a contact was sent a Marketing communication. The director is only interested in whole units. Which function should be used to return a date for calculating the difference?
sourceExplanation: TODAY() is the correct function because it returns the current date (without time), which is ideal for calculating the difference in whole days since a marketing communication was sent. Example formula: TODAY() - Last_Marketing_Communication__c This returns the number of days elapsed as a whole number. Why the other options are incorrect: DATEVALUE(): Converts a date/time or text value to a date; not needed if you already want today’s date. NOW(): Returns the current date and time, which includes hours and minutes; using it would return fractional days rather than whole days. DATETIMEVALUE(): Converts text to a date/time value; unnecessary for simply calculating days elapsed.

stem: A new app builder on the Cloud Kicks team is getting familiar with the data Model. They want to see how standard objects and custom objects relate. Which functionality should the app builder use to view these relationships?
sourceExplanation: Schema Builder is the correct functionality.
