It provides a visual representation of all standard and custom objects, including their fields and relationships (lookup and master-detail). App builders can use it to explore the data model and understand how objects are connected. Why the other options are incorrect: Object Manager: Shows object details and fields, but does not provide a visual map of relationships. Fields & Relationships: Lists fields within an object, but does not show connections between objects. Lightning App Builder: Used for creating and customizing record pages, apps, and components, not for viewing data model relationships.

stem: The marketing director is concerned that too many car parts were given Away for free last year. Which functionality should be used to ensure all free parts receive the marketing Directors' sign-off?
sourceExplanation: Approval Process is the correct functionality. It allows the marketing director to review and approve any record (in this case, free car parts) before the record can proceed or be finalized. An approval process can be configured to route records automatically to the director based on criteria (e.g., Part Type = Free). Ensures compliance and accountability for all free giveaways. Why the other options are incorrect: Chatter approval: Chatter posts are primarily for collaboration and notifications; they do not enforce formal approvals. Slack post: Slack messages can notify the director but cannot enforce approval or prevent further action. Automated email message: Emails inform the director but do not enforce approval workflows before records are finalized.

stem: Universal Containers is adding drone delivery to service offerings. The Developer wrote and tested the code and the change set is ready to go. However, the Deployment window will occur when the developer is on vacation. What can the app builder do to help ensure the code will successfully deploy to Production?

options.text: Remove Apex classes from inbound change set.

sourceExplanation: Validate the outbound change set is the correct solution. Validation allows you to test the deployment in Production without actually committing changes. This ensures that all components, including Apex classes and triggers, will compile and pass tests before the scheduled deployment. It’s especially useful when the developer is unavailable during the deployment window, providing confidence that the deployment will succeed. Why the other options are incorrect: Remove Apex classes from inbound change set: Removing Apex classes defeats the purpose of deploying the new functionality and is not a solution to deployment readiness. Use a metadata package set: Not applicable here; change sets are being used, and packages are a different deployment mechanism. Validate the inbound change set: Inbound change set validation occurs after it has been uploaded to Production; validating the outbound change set beforehand ensures readiness before the deployment window.

stem: Universal Containers manages leads in a Lead qualification queue where sales reps can accept ownership of the Lead. Campaign members are required to have a sales owner. What validation rule should an app builder configure?
sourceExplanation: The correct validation rule is AND(ISNEW(), ISBLANK(Lead.Owner:User.Id)). ISNEW(): Ensures the rule only triggers when a Lead is being created. ISBLANK(Lead.Owner:User.Id): Checks that the Lead does not have a user assigned (meaning it is still owned by a queue). This prevents new Leads from being saved without a specific sales owner, enforcing the requirement that Campaign Members always have a sales owner, while still allowing Leads to be temporarily placed in a queue until a sales rep claims them. This approach is more accurate than using NOT(ISBLANK(Lead.Owner:Queue.Id)), because that option would block any Lead from being owned by a queue, which is not desired during the qualification process.

stem: Cloud Kicks has created a custom object called Interests which is joined to Accounts by way of a junction object called Account Interest. What is the impact to users attempting to view an Account and the associated Account Interest records if they are without read access to the Interest object?

options.text: Users will be able to view the Account Interest records and will have read-only access to the Interest Records.
Users will be unable to view Account records that have a related Account Interest recor
Users will be unable to view the Account Interest records or the Interest records.
Users will be able to view the Account Interest record, but unable to view the field or any Information relating to the Interest recor

sourceExplanation: Users will be able to view the Account Interest record, but unable to view the field or any Information relating to the Interest record is correct. Why: In a junction object scenario, access to the junction record itself is controlled by the junction object's permissions. However, any fields that reference the related object (Interest) will not display data if the user lacks read access to the Interest object. Users can still see the Account Interest record exists and any fields that belong directly to the junction object, but cannot see details from the Interest object. Why the other options are incorrect: Users will be able to view the Account Interest records and will have read-only access to the Interest Records: Incorrect because read access to the Interest object is required to see its fields. Users will be unable to view Account records that have a related Account Interest record: Incorrect; Account visibility is independent of junction object access. Users will be unable to view the Account Interest records or the Interest records: Incorrect; users can still view the junction records themselves, just not the related Interest details.

stem: Universal Containers wants to improve the process to create Opportunity records related to an Account. Many fields can be populated Based on the Account record Some fields require input from the user. What should an app builder configure to meet the requirement?

options.text: Quick Action on the Account object
Assignment rule triggered from Account update
Quick Action on the Opportunity object.
Assignment rule triggered from Opportunity update

sourceExplanation: Quick Action on the Account object is the correct solution. A Quick Action on the Account object can be configured as a “Create a Record” action to create a new Opportunity. Fields on the Opportunity can be prepopulated with values from the Account, while still allowing the user to enter additional required information. This streamlines the Opportunity creation process directly from the Account record page. Why the other options are incorrect: Assignment rule triggered from Account update: Assignment rules are used to assign ownership of records, not to create new related records. Quick Action on the Opportunity object: Quick Actions on the Opportunity object cannot prepopulate fields from the parent Account; they are meant for creating Opportunities independently. Assignment rule triggered from Opportunity update: Again, assignment rules only handle record assignment, not field prepopulation or user input for creating new records.

stem: A customer service representative at a call center wants to be able to Collect information from customers using a series of question prompts. What should an app builder use to accomplish this?
sourceExplanation: Salesforce Flow allows the creation of guided, interactive screens where users can collect information step by step. Ideal for call center scenarios, where a customer service representative needs to follow a series of questions to gather data efficiently. Flows can include logic, branching, and data updates, making them much more powerful than simple page layouts or rules. Why the other options are incorrect: Approval Process: Used to route records for approval; not designed for interactive data collection. Path: Provides guidance through record stages but does not collect input interactively. Validation Rule: Prevents invalid data entry, but does not guide users or collect information.

stem: Which three standard component types are available in the Lightning App Builder?

options.text: custom fields for the Galactic Vendors's location: Filter list

sourceExplanation: In Lightning App Builder, standard components are prebuilt building blocks you can drag onto a page. The three correct standard component types from your list are: Recent Items: Displays the most recently viewed records for the object. Rich Text: Allows you to add formatted text, images, and links to the page. Report Chart / Report Details: Can display a chart or summarized data from a report directly on the page. Why the other options are incorrect: Custom fields for the Galactic Vendors' location: Filter list: Not a standard component; this describes a custom field or filter, not a Lightning standard component. Plain text: There is no separate “Plain Text” component; Salesforce provides Rich Text for all text display needs.

stem: What is one limitation of using schema builder when creating a Field?

options.text: Cannot add fields to page layouts.
Cannot see existing relationships between objects.

sourceExplanation: Schema Builder allows you to create custom fields, lookup/master-detail relationships, and view object relationships visually. Limitation: It does not support creating formula fields. Formula fields must be created through Object Manager. Why the other options are incorrect: Cannot create lookup relationships: Incorrect — Schema Builder can create lookup and master-detail relationships. Cannot add fields to page layouts: Incorrect — Schema Builder manages fields and relationships only; page layout assignment is done in Object Manager. Cannot see existing relationships between objects: Incorrect — Schema Builder visually displays all relationships, including lookups and master-detail.

stem: Universal Containers wants to give sales managers the ability to quickly provide sign off On an Opportunity via the Opportunity record page when a sales rep has discounted a deal by 20% To 30%. Which two features should be used for this requirement?
sourceExplanation: The correct features are: 1. Dynamic Actions: Allows adding a Quick Action (e.g., “Approve Discount”) directly on the Opportunity record page. The action can be made visible only when the discount is between 20% and 30%, using component visibility rules. 2. Approval Process: Ensures a formal record approval workflow for significant discounts. Can be triggered via the Quick Action created with Dynamic Actions, allowing sales managers to sign off on the Opportunity directly from the record page. Why the other options are incorrect: Schema Builder: Used for viewing and managing object relationships and fields; does not provide actions or approvals. Validation Rule: Prevents data entry or enforces field constraints; cannot provide a way for managers to approve discounts.

stem: When a deal is closed-won, it has to be approved by the owner's Manager prior to being added to the leaderboard for a quarterly sales Competition. An opportunity is won on the last day of the quarter and the Manager is on vacation. What is recommended to ensure all of the appropriate deals are reviewed and the leaderboard is up to date?

options.text: Have the manager's assistant reassign the approval request.
Use a quick action to forward the approval request to the next level approver.
Set up a delegated approver for the manager.
Use an assignment rule to automatically assign a delegated approver.

sourceExplanation: Set up a delegated approver for the manager is the correct solution. Delegated Approvers allow a backup approver to act on behalf of the manager when they are unavailable (e.g., on vacation). This ensures that closed-won opportunities are approved on time and can be included in the leaderboard for the quarterly sales competition. Delegated approvers can approve or reject records just like the original approver. Why the other options are incorrect: Have the manager's assistant reassign the approval request: Manual reassignment is reactive and error-prone; it requires someone to monitor approvals constantly. Use a quick action to forward the approval request to the next level approver: Quick actions cannot automatically reroute approval requests based on unavailability. Use an assignment rule to automatically assign a delegated approver: Assignment rules control record ownership, not approval routing; they cannot substitute for a delegated approver in an approval process.

stem: Universal Containers has a custom picklist called Support Level On the Account object. They would like to the real-time value of Support Level on all case records. How should an app builder implement this requirement?

options.text: Create a formula field on the Account object using the ISPICKVAL function.
Create a Lookup Relationship on the Case object.
Create a roll-up summary field using Support Level on the Account object.
Create a formula field on the Case object using the TEXT function.

sourceExplanation: Creating a formula field on the Case object using the TEXT function allows the Case to display the real-time value of the Support Level from the related Account. The formula dynamically pulls the picklist value from the Account, ensuring Cases always reflect the current Support Level. No additional automation is required, and the value updates automatically when the Account’s Support Level changes. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a formula field on the Account object using the ISPICKVAL function: ISPICKVAL evaluates picklist values but does not push the value to Case; the formula must be on the Case object to display it there. Create a Lookup Relationship on the Case object: A lookup only creates a relationship; it does not display the Support Level on the Case. Create a roll-up summary field using Support Level on the Account object: Roll-up summary fields only work for child records summarizing parent data, not for displaying picklist values on related records.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) requires that all users specify a Contract is sent on each Opportunity prior to marking it as "Closed Won". UC wants to be able to report on how many Opportunities have sent Contracts compared to how many have a missing contract when the Opportunities close. Which field type should an app builder configure to fulfill this requirement?
sourceExplanation: Checkbox is the correct field type. A checkbox field (e.g., "Contract Sent") allows users to indicate yes/no whether a contract has been sent. This field can be made required via a validation rule when an Opportunity is marked Closed Won, ensuring compliance. Checkboxes are easy to report on, enabling metrics like “Opportunities with contract sent” vs. “Opportunities missing contract.” Why the other options are incorrect: Picklist: Can store values like "Yes/No," but adds unnecessary complexity for a simple true/false scenario. Text: Not ideal for yes/no data; harder to enforce consistent input and report on. Text Area: Intended for freeform notes; cannot be used effectively for reporting on a simple binary requirement.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) is finding sales reps are inconsistent in data Entry when deals are won. CK requires that custom shoes are shipped Within two weeks after the close date. A custom field called Scheduled Ship Date on the opportunity records the ship date. How should the app builder ensure this field is properly filled out beforeSetting the opportunity to closed won?
sourceExplanation: The correct validation rule is: OR( ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won") && (Scheduled_Ship_Date__c - CloseDate) > 14, ISBLANK(Scheduled_Ship_Date__c) ) ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won") ensures the rule only triggers when the Opportunity is being set to Closed Won. (Scheduled_Ship_Date__c - CloseDate) > 14 checks that the scheduled ship date is within two weeks of the close date. ISBLANK(Scheduled_Ship_Date__c) ensures the field is not left empty. This rule prevents users from closing the Opportunity without a valid ship date within the required timeframe. Why the other options are incorrect: Option 2: Incorrect syntax (& instead of && and comparison logic is incomplete). Option 3: Incorrect calculation syntax; missing operator between Scheduled_Ship_Date__c and CloseDate. Option 1: Same as the correct answer, but if written without proper parentheses, it may cause formula errors. The recommended syntax is clear and properly formatted.

stem: An app builder wants to create a custom object and 10 fields. What should they use to create the object, fields, and relationships quickly From one place?
sourceExplanation: Schema Builder allows an app builder to create a custom object, add multiple fields, and define relationships visually in one place. It provides a drag-and-drop interface, making it faster to set up several fields and relationships without navigating through multiple screens. Why the other options are incorrect: Lightning Object Creator: Quickly creates objects and fields but is more suited for simple objects with fewer fields; Schema Builder is better for visualizing relationships and bulk field creation. Manage Field Permissions: Used only to control who can view or edit fields, not for creating them. Developer Console: Used for writing Apex code or running queries, not for creating objects or fields visually.

stem: Universal Containers asked the app builder to ensure when an Account type changes to 'Past-Customer' the contacts directly related to That account get an updated status of 'Re-Market'. Which automation should the app builder use to accomplish this task?
sourceExplanation: A record-triggered flow can run automatically when an Account record is updated. It can check if the Account Type changes to “Past-Customer” and then update all related Contacts with a Status of “Re-Market”. This provides a declarative, automated approach without needing custom code. Why the other options are incorrect: Validation Rule: Prevents or enforces data entry rules but cannot update related records automatically. Lightning Component: Used to create custom UI components, not for automated updates to related records. Screen Flow: Requires manual user interaction, so it would not automatically update contacts when the account type changes.

stem: A sales manager has noticed that reps continue to input contacts Directly in their phone instead of adding them to Salesforce. What should an app builder recommend to ensure the data makes it into Salesforce?

options.text: Allow Salesforce to import Contacts from mobile device Contact lists.
Enable in-app notifications every time a contact is create
Enable offline create, edit, and delete in Salesforce for Android and iOS.
Allow users to relate a contact to multiple accounts.

sourceExplanation: Allow Salesforce to import Contacts from mobile device Contact lists is the correct solution. This enables the Salesforce mobile app to sync contacts from users’ phone contact lists directly into Salesforce. Ensures new contacts created on mobile devices automatically appear in Salesforce, maintaining data consistency. Reduces the risk of lost or untracked contacts that are only stored on personal devices. Why the other options are incorrect: Enable in-app notifications every time a contact is created: Notifications alert users but do not automatically import contacts. Enable offline create, edit, and delete in Salesforce for Android and iOS: Supports offline work within Salesforce only; it does not capture contacts created outside Salesforce. Allow users to relate a contact to multiple accounts: Manages relationships between contacts and accounts but does not ensure external contacts are added to Salesforce.

stem: Cloud Kicks is implementing an approval process for opportunities that requires managers To approve all opportunities above $50,000 before they can be marked as Closed Won. Which two delivery methods can a manager utilize to respond to approval requests in the Salesforce Mobile app?
sourceExplanation: The correct delivery methods are: 1. In-App Notification: Managers receive real-time alerts within the Salesforce mobile app when an approval request is assigned. They can review and approve or reject the request directly from the notification. 2. Record Detail: Managers can open the Opportunity record from the mobile app and see the approval request section. From there, they can approve or reject the request while viewing the full record context. Why the other options are incorrect: Navigation Menu: Used to access different apps or items in Salesforce, not for responding to approval requests directly. Home Screen: Displays dashboards and recent items but does not provide interactive approval actions.

stem: The marketing team at Universal Containers has a list of 400 leads it wants to upload to Salesforce. The team needs to avoid creating duplicate records. Which two actions should be taken to meet this requirement?

options.text: Use Data Loader's update function to import leads and match to existing Records based on e- mail address.
Upload the lead list using the Import Wizard and select a Matching Type to Prevent duplicate lead creation.
Enable Duplicate Matching in the Data Management section in Setup and Activate the Lead-to-Lead scenario.
Utilize a Lead Matching Rule and corresponding Duplicate Rule to block newly Created duplicate leads.

sourceExplanation: The correct actions are: 1. Utilize a Lead Matching Rule and corresponding Duplicate Rule to block newly created duplicate leads: Matching rules define how Salesforce identifies potential duplicates (e.g., based on email or name). Duplicate rules enforce actions when a duplicate is detected, such as blocking creation or allowing an alert. This ensures that importing new leads does not create duplicates. 2. Upload the lead list using the Import Wizard and select a Matching Type to prevent duplicate lead creation: The Import Wizard allows specifying a matching field (like email) to check for existing records. Prevents creating duplicate leads during the import process. Why the other options are incorrect: Use Data Loader’s update function to import leads and match to existing records based on email address: The update function only updates existing records, it does not prevent duplicates if new records are inserted. Enable Duplicate Matching in the Data Management section in Setup and activate the Lead-to-Lead scenario: Activating a matching scenario alone does not prevent duplicates; duplicate rules must also be configured to enforce the action.

stem: An app builder at DreamHouse Realty created a custom object which has Fields containing data from two different objects via related lookups. What is needed to create "with" or "without" reports on the new custom Object?
sourceExplanation: Custom Report Type is the correct solution. To create reports that show records “with” or “without” related data from other objects, a Custom Report Type (CRT) is required. CRTs allow you to define primary and related objects and configure the report to include records with or without related records. This is essential when the custom object has lookup relationships and you want full reporting flexibility. Why the other options are incorrect: Report Filters: Only limit the records displayed; they cannot change the scope to include/exclude related records. Row-Level Formula: Calculates values for each row in a report but does not affect which records are included. Report Bucket Field: Groups data into buckets for reporting purposes but cannot include/exclude records based on related objects.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) has a time-sensitive need for a custom Component to be built in 4 weeks. UC developers require additional Enablement to complete the work and are logged by several months. Which option should an app builder suggest to meet this requirement?
sourceExplanation: Use an AppExchange solution is the correct choice. AppExchange offers prebuilt, tested components that can often be installed and configured quickly. This allows UC to meet time-sensitive requirements without waiting for internal developers to gain enablement or build a custom component from scratch. Ideal when a solution is needed within weeks rather than months. Why the other options are incorrect: Build a screen flow page: Flows can automate processes and collect data but cannot fully replace a custom Lightning component with all UI and functionality needs. Build a Lightning record page: Record pages organize components but do not create new functionality; a custom component is still needed. Use a Bolt solution: Bolt solutions are templates for Communities (Experience Cloud), not for adding a custom component to Salesforce quickly.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) has a custom Invoice object and a custom Invoice Line Item Object. The Invoice Line Item object has a lookup relationship to the Invoice. UC would like to Convert the lookup relationship to a master-detail relationship but is unable to do so. Which two reasons could be preventing this relationship conversion?

options.text: There are already two master-detail relationships on the Invoice Line Item.
Custom objects are unable to be on the detail side of a master-detail Relationship.
Invoice Line Item records exist without having the Invoice lookup field Populate
There is a roll-up summary field on the Invoice object.

sourceExplanation: The two reasons preventing the conversion to a master-detail relationship are: 1. Invoice Line Item records exist without having the Invoice lookup field populated: Master-detail relationships require that every child record has a parent. If some Invoice Line Item records do not reference an Invoice, Salesforce cannot enforce the master-detail constraint. 2. There are already two master-detail relationships on the Invoice Line Item: Salesforce limits custom objects to two master-detail relationships. If both slots are already used, you cannot create a new master-detail relationship until one is removed. Why the other options are incorrect: Custom objects are unable to be on the detail side of a master-detail relationship: Incorrect — custom objects can be on the detail side of a master-detail relationship. There is a roll-up summary field on the Invoice object: Roll-up summary fields exist on the master and do not prevent creating a master-detail relationship from the child.

stem: Universal Containers generates leads from three different Sources: web, trade shows, and partners. Some of the information Collected is applicable to all sources, there is also information that is unique To each type of lead What should an app builder configure to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create three lead record types each with its own page layout containing the relevant Fields.
Create three sections on the lead layout and instruct users to collapse the non- Relevant fields.
Create a lead object on the partner community and a record type for web and trade leads.
Create custom objects for each type of lead with each page layout only containing the Relevant fields.

sourceExplanation: Create three lead record types, each with its own page layout containing the relevant fields is the correct solution. Record types allow customizing page layouts for different business processes or sources (web, trade show, partner). Each record type can display only the fields relevant to that lead source while sharing common fields across all types. This approach maintains a single Lead object and simplifies reporting and management. Why the other options are incorrect: Create three sections on the lead layout and instruct users to collapse the non-relevant fields: Users may ignore instructions; this approach does not enforce data entry rules. Create a lead object on the partner community and a record type for web and trade leads: Creating a separate object is unnecessary and complicates reporting, as all leads should remain in one object. Create custom objects for each type of lead with each page layout only containing the relevant fields: Using multiple objects adds unneeded complexity, breaking standard lead processes and reports.

stem: Universal Containers has a Lightning record page that supportsBoth the mobile app and desktop. An app builder has downloaded a custom Lightning component from AppExchange, but users are unable to view the Component on mobile devices.

options.text: The component needs to be activate
The record page template is unable to support mobile devices.
The component has been developed for Desktop Pages.
The record page needs to be activate

sourceExplanation: Some AppExchange Lightning components are designed to work only on desktop Lightning pages and will not render on mobile devices. This is why users cannot see the component in the Salesforce mobile app even though it appears on desktop. Why the other options are incorrect: The component needs to be activated: Activation affects the page layout visibility, but if the component is desktop-only, activation alone won’t make it appear on mobile. The record page template is unable to support mobile devices: Standard Lightning record page templates support both desktop and mobile, so this is unlikely the issue. The record page needs to be activated: Similar to component activation, page activation ensures visibility, but does not resolve a desktop-only component limitation.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to summarize the number of open Cases related to an Account, as well As the number of closed Cases to indicate whether customer support utilization is high, medium, or Low. Two number fields have been created: NUM_open_Cases_c and NUM_Closed Cases_. Which two solutions meet these business requirements?
sourceExplanation: Apex is correct because custom logic in Apex can be written to compute and summarize the number of open and closed cases related to an Account. Apex can perform complex calculations and update custom fields like NUM_open_Cases_c and NUM_Closed_Cases_ based on specific criteria, allowing Cloud Kicks to track and categorize customer support utilization efficiently. AppExchange is correct because there are various pre-built applications and packages available on the Salesforce AppExchange that can provide the functionality to track and summarize open and closed cases. These apps may include reporting or automation tools that can be configured to categorize support utilization. Why the other options are incorrect: Validation Rule: Validation Rules are used to enforce data integrity and ensure that records meet certain criteria before being saved. They are not used for calculations or summarizing data like the number of open or closed cases. Approval Process: Approval Processes are used to automate the approval of records in Salesforce (e.g., opportunities, requests) and are not meant for summarizing case data or categorizing customer support utilization.

stem: accounts to discuss various topics. CK would like all company employees to see these Conversations. Which two features of Chatter would meet CK's business needs?

options.text: Set up new public Chatter groups.
Set up new private Chatter groups.
Use Chatter actions to create tasks to complete.
Use post action on the Account object.

sourceExplanation: Set up new public Chatter groups is correct because public Chatter groups allow all employees in the organization to join and participate in conversations around a specific topic. In this case, creating public groups for each customer account or related topic would enable CK's employees to collaborate and discuss various subjects in an open space that everyone can see and contribute to. Use post action on the Account object is correct because Chatter posts can be made directly on records, such as the Account object. By using the "Post" action, CK employees can leave comments, share updates, and have discussions specifically related to the Customer accounts. These posts will be visible to all employees, if the settings allow it, promoting collaboration around customer accounts. Why the other options are incorrect: Set up new private Chatter groups: Private Chatter groups restrict participation to a defined set of users. While they can be used for more focused discussions, they don't meet the requirement for all employees to see the conversations. Private groups limit visibility, so they wouldn’t be suitable for CK's goal of universal collaboration. Use Chatter actions to create tasks to complete: Chatter actions are designed for creating tasks, events, or other actions tied to records. While useful for task management, they don’t directly facilitate open, company-wide discussions. This option doesn’t specifically address CK's goal of socializing and collaborating around customer accounts.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to display the number of opportunities that Are Closed Won with a Close Date within the last year on the Account detail Page. What should an app builder use to implement this?
sourceExplanation: Roll-up summary field is the correct solution because it allows an app builder to aggregate data from related child records (in this case, Opportunities) and display that aggregated data on the parent record (in this case, the Account). A roll-up summary field can be configured to count the number of Closed Won opportunities with a Close Date within the last year, meeting Cloud Kicks' requirement to show this information on the Account detail page. Why the other options are incorrect: Activity timeline: The Activity Timeline is used to display activities and interactions (like tasks and events) related to a record, but it doesn't aggregate data such as counting opportunities or filtering based on criteria like Closed Won status or Close Date. Formula field: Formula fields allow for the calculation of values based on other fields, but they cannot aggregate related records (like counting related Opportunities). They are not suitable for summarizing data across child records. Validation rule: Validation rules are used to enforce data integrity by ensuring that certain conditions are met before a record is saved. They are not used for displaying or aggregating data on the Account detail page.

stem: Universal Containers uses the Asset object to track products that Are installed at customer locations. A new object, Asset Inventory, has Been created to capture details about the asset. Which approach should the app builder take to Asset Inventory as a Related list on Asset?

options.text: Create a lookup relationship on Asset Inventory to Asset. Add the Asset Inventory Related list to the Asset page layout.
Create a roll-up on Asset. Add the Asset Inventory related list to the Asset page Layout.
Create a master-detail relationship on Asset to Asset Inventory Add the Asset Inventory related list to the Asset page layout.
Create a junction object to relate Asset Inventory and Asset. Add the Asset Inventory Related list to the Asset page layout.

sourceExplanation: Create a lookup relationship on Asset Inventory to Asset. Add the Asset Inventory related list to the Asset page layout. is the correct approach because a lookup relationship is appropriate when you want to relate two objects without enforcing a parent-child hierarchy (unlike a master-detail relationship). In this case, Asset Inventory is capturing details about assets, but you don’t need to enforce strong ownership, and a lookup relationship will allow the Asset Inventory to be associated with specific Assets. After creating this relationship, you can add the Asset Inventory related list to the Asset page layout to display the related Asset Inventory records. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a roll-up on Asset. Add the Asset Inventory related list to the Asset page layout: A roll-up summary field is used for aggregating data from child records to a parent record (like summing or counting related records). However, it is only available for master-detail relationships, and Asset Inventory is not being set up as a master-detail relationship here. Therefore, a roll-up summary is not appropriate. Create a master-detail relationship on Asset to Asset Inventory. Add the Asset Inventory related list to the Asset page layout: This approach would enforce strict parent-child behavior, where Asset Inventory would be tightly tied to the Asset record (with record deletion cascading). While this could work, it's typically not necessary unless you require this level of data integrity and need to enforce ownership, which is not specified in the question. Create a junction object to relate Asset Inventory and Asset. Add the Asset Inventory related list to the Asset page layout: A junction object is used to create a many-to-many relationship between two objects. In this case, a junction object is unnecessary because there’s only a one-to-many relationship between Asset and Asset Inventory (each Asset can have many Asset Inventory records). Using a junction object would overcomplicate the relationship.

stem: DreamHouse Realty has a mentorship program that pairs Experienced Realtors with new Realtors. Each experienced Realtor can Mentor one or several new Realtors, and each new Realtor is required to Work with a single experienced Realtor they report to for a probationary Perio Which type of relationship would an app builder set up to meet this Specification?
sourceExplanation: Lookup relationship is the correct choice because it allows for a one-to-many relationship where each new Realtor can be associated with a single experienced Realtor (the one they report to during their probationary period). In this case, the experienced Realtor can be linked to one or multiple new Realtors, but each new Realtor can only have one experienced Realtor that they report to. A lookup relationship is ideal for this use case because: One experienced Realtor can mentor multiple new Realtors (the experienced Realtor is the “parent” record, and the new Realtor is the “child”). Each new Realtor works with one experienced Realtor (each new Realtor is “linked” to exactly one experienced Realtor, but the relationship is not strictly hierarchical like a master-detail relationship). Why the other options are incorrect: Indirect lookup: This type of relationship is used when an external object (e.g., external data) needs to be related to a Salesforce object using a unique identifier, which doesn’t apply to this scenario of mentoring within Salesforce. Many-to-many: This would require a junction object, but the use case described is a one-to-many relationship (one experienced Realtor can have multiple new Realtors, but each new Realtor works with only one experienced Realtor). A many-to-many relationship is unnecessary and overly complex in this case. Master-detail: This type of relationship enforces a strict parent-child structure, where the child record’s existence is dependent on the parent (the child is automatically deleted if the parent is deleted). This would not be appropriate for this case, as the relationship between experienced and new Realtors does not require such strict coupling. A lookup relationship is more suitable here because the new Realtor can exist independently and doesn’t require the strict data integrity enforced by master-detail.

stem: An app builder wants to streamline the user experience by reflecting summarized calculations of Specific fields on various objects. Which three field types can be used in roll-up summary fields to accomplish this?
sourceExplanation: Checkbox, Currency, and Percent are the correct field types that can be used in roll-up summary fields to reflect summarized calculations across related records. Here's why each is valid: Checkbox: Roll-up summary fields can count the number of child records that meet specific criteria, such as a checkbox being marked as TRUE. For example, you could count the number of related records where a checkbox field is selected. Currency: You can use roll-up summary fields to aggregate (sum, average, min, max) currency fields from child records. This is useful for summing values like sales, revenue, or amounts across related records (e.g., summing opportunity amounts related to an account). Percent: Similar to currency fields, roll-up summary fields can also be used to calculate aggregated values from percentage fields in child records. For example, you can calculate the average or sum of percent values for related records. Why the other options are incorrect: Time: Time fields cannot be used in roll-up summary fields for direct aggregation like sum or average. While you can use Time fields in reports or other calculations, they are not supported in roll-up summary fields for aggregation. Date: Date fields can be used for filtering records in a roll-up summary field but are not supported for direct summarization (e.g., summing or averaging) within a roll-up summary. You can filter or use date ranges, but you cannot aggregate date fields in a roll-up summary.

stem: An app builder wants to update a field on the parent record When a child record connected via lookup is delete Which automation should the app builder use?
sourceExplanation: Record-triggered flow is the correct solution because it allows automation to trigger when a child record is deleted and can then perform updates to the parent record. With a record-triggered flow, the app builder can specify that when a child record connected via a lookup relationship is deleted, the flow will update the corresponding parent record accordingly. This type of flow is ideal for situations where you need to automatically trigger updates based on the creation, update, or deletion of records, including updates to the parent record when the child is deleted. Why the other options are incorrect: Validation rule: Validation rules are used to enforce data integrity before a record is saved, ensuring that certain conditions are met. They do not allow automation on record deletion or update actions like the one needed here. Autolaunched flow: Autolaunched flows can be used to automate processes, but they need to be triggered explicitly (e.g., via Apex, a button, or a scheduled action). They cannot automatically trigger upon the deletion of a child record, which is why a record-triggered flow is more appropriate for this use case. Quick action: Quick actions are typically used for initiating actions from the user interface, such as creating records or launching flows. They are not designed to automatically trigger processes based on the deletion of records. While quick actions can be useful in certain automation contexts, they would require user intervention, which does not fit the scenario of automating the update upon record deletion.

stem: At Ursa Solar Major, only users with the Outer Planets profile Need to see the Jupiter field on the Solar System object. How should the app builder satisfy this requirement?
sourceExplanation: Field-level security is the correct solution because it allows the app builder to control visibility and access to specific fields based on a user's profile. In this case, the app builder can configure field-level security to ensure that only users with the Outer Planets profile can see the Jupiter field on the Solar System object. This approach allows precise control over which profiles can view or edit specific fields. Why the other options are incorrect: Classic encryption: Classic encryption is used to protect sensitive data at rest by encrypting fields in Salesforce. While it provides security for sensitive data, it is not used for controlling field visibility based on user profiles. It is unrelated to the use case of restricting field visibility to specific profiles. Filtered view: A filtered view generally refers to filtering data within a report or a list view, but it does not control visibility of individual fields. It would not be appropriate for restricting access to a specific field like the Jupiter field. Sharing rules: Sharing rules control record-level access, such as which users or groups can view or edit records based on record ownership or criteria. They do not apply to controlling access to specific fields within a record. Therefore, sharing rules would not be suitable for limiting visibility of a particular field like the Jupiter field.

stem: The Universal Containers data manager has been complaining About the lack of data integrity on Contact records. Sales reps have not been filling out the Region fiel. The data manager Wants the Region field filled out only for Contacts that are associated to Accounts that have been marked as 'High Priority' on the Customer Status Field. What can the app builder do to fulfil this requirement?

options.text: Create a validation rule on Account.
Make the Customer Status field required on Account.
Create a validation rule on Contact.
Make the Region field required on Contact.

sourceExplanation: Create a validation rule on Contact is the correct solution because the goal is to ensure that the Region field is filled out only when the Contact is associated with an Account marked as "High Priority" in the Customer Status field. A validation rule on the Contact object can be written to check whether the associated Account has the "High Priority" status and ensure that the Region field is not blank. If the conditions are met (the Account is high priority), the Region field will be required. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a validation rule on Account: Validation rules on the Account object would not directly solve the problem of requiring the Region field on Contacts. Validation rules should be placed on the object where the field exists (in this case, the Contact object), and the rule needs to be based on the relationship between Contact and Account. Make the Customer Status field required on Account: Making the Customer Status field required on the Account object does not address the issue of ensuring the Region field is filled out on the Contact record. It would only ensure that the Account’s Customer Status is always filled out, but it would not guarantee the required Region field for Contacts. Make the Region field required on Contact: Making the Region field required on Contact would force users to fill out the field, but it doesn't specify that the Region field should only be required when the Contact is associated with an Account marked as "High Priority." This would apply the rule universally, not just under specific conditions. A validation rule would allow the Region field to be required only under the specified condition (when the associated Account is "High Priority").

stem: An app builder wants to add the option to 'Send New Email' from Leads, Contacts, and Accounts for users on mobile. What is the benefit of using global actions to accomplish this?

options.text: The global action's layout automatically clones the default page layout.
Salesforce Lightning Component Library houses existing global actions prebuilt for use.
Global actions are record-specific and are available when searching that particular Object.
Global actions can be accessed anywhere actions are available in mobile including Record detail pages, feed, and Chatter groups.

sourceExplanation: Global actions can be accessed anywhere actions are available in mobile, including record detail pages, feed, and Chatter groups is the correct answer. Global actions in Salesforce provide a flexible and accessible way to perform actions from virtually anywhere in the app, including mobile devices. These actions can be initiated from record pages (such as Lead, Contact, or Account detail pages), the Chatter feed, or other locations in the Salesforce mobile interface. This ensures that users can quickly and easily initiate actions, such as sending a new email, without having to navigate through multiple screens or pages. Why the other options are incorrect: The global action's layout automatically clones the default page layout: This is incorrect because global actions don't automatically clone or replicate a page layout. Instead, they are designed with custom layouts and can be customized by the app builder to suit specific business needs. Page layouts are a different concept, focused on how fields and components are displayed on record pages, whereas global actions allow users to initiate actions without needing a specific page context. Salesforce Lightning Component Library houses existing global actions prebuilt for use: While the Lightning Component Library does house a variety of pre-built components that can be used in the UI, global actions themselves are not stored there. Instead, global actions are configured and managed in the Salesforce setup menu. This option is misleading because global actions are not typically categorized in the Lightning Component Library. Global actions are record-specific and are available when searching that particular Object: This is incorrect because global actions are not record-specific; they are designed to be global and available throughout the Salesforce environment, including various objects, feeds, and pages. Record-specific actions are more tightly integrated with specific objects and data but are not as broadly accessible as global actions.

stem: Ursa Major Solar (UMS) uses Cases to track customer Complaints, an Issue _c object to represent known problems with its solar Panels, and a Case_Issue_c junction object to relate known problems to Customer complaints. Periodically, UMS conducts audits which require the Auditing users to view case_Issue_c records. Which access levels must be configured to allow UMS users to access Case Issue_c records?

options.text: Read-Only access on Case and Issue_c
Read-Only access on Case and Case Issue_e
Read-Only access on Issue_c and Case Issue_c

sourceExplanation: Read-Only access on Issue_c and Case_Issue_c is the correct access level that must be configured to allow UMS users to access Case_Issue_c records. Here's why: Issue_c is the object that represents known problems with the solar panels. For users to view the related records in Case_Issue_c, they need access to Issue_c records, as Case_Issue_c is a junction object that connects the two (Cases and Issues). Case_Issue_c is the junction object that relates Cases to Issue_c records. To view these junction records, users must have access to Case_Issue_c itself, even though they may not need to modify it. Providing Read-Only access to both Issue_c and Case_Issue_c ensures users can view the necessary information without the ability to make any changes. Why the other options are incorrect: Read-Only access on Case and Issue_c: This option only grants access to the Case and Issue_c objects but does not give the necessary access to Case_Issue_c, the junction object.
