stem: Where can an app builder edit an existing app to add Components to the utility bar?
sourceExplanation: App Manager is the correct location where an app builder can edit an existing app to add components to the utility bar. The App Manager is the central place for managing apps in Salesforce, and it allows you to modify the components of an app, including adding components to the utility bar. From App Manager, you can select the app you want to modify, then edit the app to customize its layout, including adding utility bar components such as quick actions, custom Lightning components, or other tools that you want to make available across all pages within that app. Why the other options are incorrect: Lightning App Builder: The Lightning App Builder is primarily used for customizing record pages, home pages, and app pages (not specifically the utility bar). It allows you to add and configure components on the page level but not on the utility bar itself. The utility bar is managed through the App Manager. Lightning Record Page: The Lightning Record Page is used to customize the layout and components on a specific record page, such as the Opportunity or Account record. While you can add components to a record page, this is not where you would edit the utility bar, which is consistent across the app. App Menu: The App Menu is the area where you access different apps, and it controls the visibility of apps within Salesforce, but it doesn't allow for customizing the utility bar or adding components to it. Correct approach: To edit and customize the utility bar, you would need to use the App Manager to modify the app and add or remove components in the utility bar.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to change a master-detail Relationship on Account to a lookup relationship with a custom object Park. The app builder tries to reconfigure this but is unable to do so. What could be causing this?

options.text: The Account is included in a flow process on the Park object.
The park records have existing formulas on the Account.
The Park object needs at least one Master-Detail field for reporting.
The Account record includes Parks roll-up summary fields.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is: The Account record includes Parks roll-up summary fields. Here's why: A roll-up summary field is a special field that aggregates data from child records (like summing, counting, or averaging fields) and displays that information on the parent record. In Salesforce, roll-up summary fields are only available on master-detail relationships, meaning they can only be used when the child record is part of a master-detail relationship. Therefore, you cannot convert a master-detail relationship to a lookup relationship if there are existing roll-up summary fields on the parent object that are aggregating data from the child records. To resolve this, the app builder would need to delete the roll-up summary field on the Account before they can change the relationship from master-detail to lookup. Why the other options are incorrect: The Account is included in a flow process on the Park object: This would not prevent the relationship change. While flows might reference the Account object, it does not block the ability to change the relationship type between Account and Park. The park records have existing formulas on the Account: Formula fields referencing the parent object (in this case, Account) do not prevent changing the relationship type from master-detail to lookup. These can still be maintained even after the change. The Park object needs at least one Master-Detail field for reporting: This is not a requirement. The Park object does not need to have a Master-Detail field to function for reporting. You can use a lookup relationship for reporting purposes, as lookup relationships can also be used to report on related objects. Summary: The presence of roll-up summary fields on the parent object (Account) is the primary reason the relationship change cannot be made. These fields rely on a master-detail relationship and must be deleted before the conversion to a lookup relationship can occur.

stem: Universal Containers created a 'New Task' custom action on the Opportunity object. The action was added to all page layouts in the Mobile & Lightning Actions section. Which Lightning component should the app builder add to the layout to Display the action?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is: Activities. Here's why: In Salesforce Lightning, mobile actions and Lightning actions (such as the "New Task" custom action) are typically displayed in the Activities section of a page layout. The Activities component is specifically designed to show tasks, events, and other activity-related actions and records. Since you've created a custom "New Task" action on the Opportunity object and added it to the page layouts in the Mobile & Lightning Actions section, you'll need to ensure that the Activities component is placed on the page layout to display those actions (including tasks, calls, events, etc.) in the UI. This section is responsible for showing and allowing users to interact with those activity-related actions. Why the other options are incorrect: Highlights panel: The Highlights Panel displays important record details (like key fields) at the top of the record page but does not display actions such as creating a new task. The Highlights Panel is focused on quick views of key information, not actions or activity-related records. Related lists: Related lists show lists of related records (such as related contacts, opportunities, cases, etc.), but they are not meant to display actions. The "New Task" action is an activity-based action, which should be placed in the Activities component rather than in a related list. Related record: This component is used to display related records, and it would not be appropriate for displaying actions like creating a new task. The Activities component is more appropriate for displaying actions like tasks, calls, and events. Summary: To display the custom "New Task" action, the app builder should add the Activities component to the Opportunity page layout. This component is designed to display activity-related actions and records, including tasks.

stem: Properly installing managed packages helps prevent conflicts With customizations made by customers and partners. Which functionality should be used to set up packages?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is: Namespace. Here's why: When you install a managed package in Salesforce, a namespace is used to ensure that the components in the package (such as custom objects, fields, classes, and other resources) don't conflict with components in the customer's Salesforce org or other managed packages. The namespace serves as a unique identifier for the package, helping to prevent naming conflicts and ensuring that the components of the managed package are kept distinct from other customizations or packages. Why the other options are incorrect: Help setting: The Help setting in Salesforce refers to the configuration of help and documentation within the app, but it has nothing to do with preventing conflicts between managed packages and customizations. It is used for providing help text or guidance to users within Salesforce, not for package management. Description: The Description field is used to provide a summary or explanation of a managed package, but it doesn't play a role in preventing conflicts between customizations or package components. It's more about providing information about the package. Allow sharing: The Allow sharing option refers to the visibility and access settings for records, such as whether a record can be shared between users or groups. This is unrelated to managed package installation or avoiding conflicts between components. It controls how data is shared, not how package components are handled. Summary: To prevent conflicts with customizations when installing managed packages, Salesforce uses a namespace, which ensures that all the components of the managed package have unique identifiers. This helps avoid clashes with existing customizations or other installed packages in the organization.

stem: After a deal is closed, Cloud Kicks (CK) wants to assign a user as A customer service manager (CSM) in addition to the account owner and Would like a new field to easily track and report which CSM is assigned to The Account. Which solution should an app builder use for this request?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is: Lookup field. Here’s why: A Lookup field allows you to associate a record from another object (in this case, a User record) with the Account. This is the ideal solution for tracking which Customer Service Manager (CSM) is assigned to an account because it provides a direct relationship between the Account and the CSM (who is a User in Salesforce). The lookup field will allow you to easily assign and report on the CSM associated with the account. With a lookup relationship, the CSM can be selected from the User object and reported on directly in reports or dashboards. This is much more efficient and useful than other types of fields, as it creates a direct reference to the User record rather than just storing text or multiple options. Why the other options are incorrect: Text field: A Text field would allow you to manually input the name of the CSM, but it doesn't create any meaningful relationship between the Account and the User. It would make it harder to report on the CSMs assigned to accounts, and it would not enforce consistency or validation (e.g., ensuring the correct CSM is assigned). It's not ideal for associating records. Picklist field: A Picklist field could be used if the app builder wants to select a predefined list of CSMs, but it is not as dynamic or flexible as a Lookup field. With a picklist, it would be cumbersome to maintain and update the list of available CSMs, especially if it changes frequently. Also, it doesn't allow for direct linking to User records, which could limit reporting and tracking. Multi-select picklist field: A Multi-select picklist field would allow you to select multiple values, but it doesn't provide a direct relationship with the User object, nor is it suitable for associating a single CSM with an Account. This approach would not be appropriate for a one-to-one relationship, which is needed for tracking a single CSM per Account. Summary: A Lookup field is the best solution because it allows you to directly associate an Account with a Customer Service Manager (CSM), making it easy to track and report on which CSM is assigned to each Account. It ensures a clean relationship and provides a flexible, dynamic solution.

stem: The app builder at Northern Trail Outfitters created a report type For opportunities with or without shipments. The operations team wants to See the account rating information on the report. What should the app builder do to fulfill this request?

options.text: Use add fields related via lookup with the view set to opportunities.
Change the account/opportunity relationship to a master/detail relationship.
Change the primary object of the custom report type to the Account object.
Add the Account Rating field to the opportunity record page.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is: Use add fields related via lookup with the view set to opportunities. Here’s why: In Salesforce, when creating a custom report type for Opportunities with or without Shipments, the app builder needs to include fields from related objects, such as Account Rating, which is on the related Account object. Since there is a lookup relationship between Opportunities and Accounts (Accounts are the parent object, and Opportunities are the child object), the app builder can use the "Add fields related via lookup" option to add the Account Rating field to the report. This allows the report to include information from the Account (such as Account Rating) while still using the Opportunity as the primary object in the report. Add fields related via lookup: In this case, the app builder can add Account Rating from the related Account object by selecting the appropriate lookup relationship between Account and Opportunity. This enables the report to show Account Rating alongside Opportunity data without changing the underlying report type structure. Why the other options are incorrect: Change the account/opportunity relationship to a master/detail relationship: This would not be necessary for displaying Account Rating in the report. In most cases, changing the relationship to a master-detail relationship isn't required unless there's a strict need for cascading delete behavior or more tightly coupled relationships. The existing lookup relationship between Opportunity and Account is sufficient for the report, and converting it to master-detail would complicate things unnecessarily. Change the primary object of the custom report type to the Account object: If the app builder changes the primary object of the report type to Account, the report would become based on Account data instead of Opportunity data. While this may allow the Account Rating field to appear, it would break the original requirement of having a report on Opportunities with or without Shipments. The report would no longer be focused on Opportunities, so this solution doesn't meet the request. Add the Account Rating field to the opportunity record page: This only affects the record page layout and does not impact the report itself. Adding the Account Rating field to the Opportunity record page would allow users to see it when viewing the Opportunity record, but it would not make that information available in a report, which is the core requirement in this case. Summary: The correct solution is to use "Add fields related via lookup" to bring the Account Rating field into the Opportunity-based report. This allows the app builder to include Account Rating from the related Account without changing the structure of the report or the relationships between the objects.

stem: Universal Container wants customers to be able to open cases From a public-facing website. What should the app builder use to enable visitors to the website?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is: Web-to-case. Here's why: Web-to-Case allows you to create cases directly from a public-facing website. This feature enables customers to submit case details via a web form, and the information is automatically captured and stored in Salesforce as a new Case record. The app builder can configure a web form that captures information such as the customer's name, contact information, and details of the issue. When the customer submits the form, a case is created in Salesforce, which can be assigned to support agents for follow-up. This is the ideal solution for allowing customers to open cases via a website. Why the other options are incorrect: Outbound Message: An Outbound Message is used in workflow rules or Process Builder to send data to external systems when certain criteria are met. It does not help in creating cases from a website. This option is focused on outbound communication, not on gathering customer data through a web interface. Screen Flow: A Screen Flow allows you to guide users through a series of steps in a UI, such as creating a case or gathering additional data. However, this would typically be used in an internal Salesforce experience, not for creating cases from a public-facing website. Screen flows are designed for use within Salesforce or in Salesforce Community pages, not directly exposed to the public internet. Email-to-Case: Email-to-Case is a feature that allows customers to send an email to a specific address (e.g., support@yourcompany.com), and Salesforce automatically converts that email into a Case. While this is a great feature for handling customer support requests via email, it does not allow customers to open cases directly from a public-facing website, which is the specific requirement in this scenario. Summary: Web-to-Case is the ideal solution because it enables customers to submit cases via a web form, which then automatically creates Cases in Salesforce. This allows customers to open cases directly from a public-facing website.

stem: Ursa Major Solar (UMS) has a custom object where they track Galactic Vendors. The object has four custom fields for the Galactic Vendors's location: • Street • City • Planet • Galaxy The UMS's leadership wants these fields to be concatenated into a single formula field on two lines. Which formula fulfills this requirement?
sourceExplanation: The correct formula is A: Street__c & BR() & City__c & ", " & Planet__c & " " & Galaxy__c Explanation: Formula Components: Street__c: The Street field (custom field, hence using __c to refer to it). BR(): This function inserts a line break between the Street and the rest of the fields, ensuring that the Street appears on the first line, followed by the other fields on the second line. City__c & ", ": The City field followed by a comma and a space for formatting. Planet__c & " ": The Planet field followed by a space. Galaxy__c: The Galaxy field. This formula combines the fields into the desired format with two lines. The first line will contain Street, and the second line will contain City, Planet, and Galaxy. Why the other options are incorrect: B. Street &(& City & ", " & Planet & " " & Galaxy): This formula contains syntax errors. The (& portion is invalid and doesn't properly concatenate the fields. The correct syntax for concatenating fields is &. C. Street & BR() & City & ", " & Planet & " " & Galaxy: This formula lacks the field names (__c). If the fields are custom, the correct format is Street__c, not just Street. Additionally, this formula assumes that the fields are non-custom, which is likely incorrect given the context. D. Street__r & BR() & City__r & ", " & Planet__r & " " & Galaxy__r: This formula is referencing related object fields, using __r instead of __c. The __r suffix is used for relationship fields (like lookup or master-detail fields) when you're referencing related objects. However, if Street, City, Planet, and Galaxy are custom fields on the Galactic Vendor object (not related to other objects), they should use the __c suffix.

stem: Universal Containers has Public Read/Write as the Account Organization-wide default (OWD) setting. Visitors to the customer Community site report that they can see all of the company's account Records. How should an app builder configure Account sharing so that community Users only see their own Account?

options.text: Create an account record type for external accounts.
Set the account external OWD to private.
Define an owner-based sharing rule for external accounts.
Define a permission set for external accounts.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is: Set the account external OWD to private. Explanation: Organization-Wide Default (OWD) settings determine the baseline level of access that users have to records in Salesforce. In this case, Public Read/Write is set for Accounts, meaning that all users can view and edit Account records unless further restrictions are applied. Community Users are likely using a Customer Community or Partner Community license, and they should only be able to see their own Account records. To restrict community users to only seeing their own Accounts, you need to adjust the External OWD for the Account object. Why this works: Set the account external OWD to private: By setting the External Sharing Model (External OWD) for the Account object to Private, you restrict visibility of Account records for external users, such as community members. This means that community users will only be able to view their own Account records and not those of other users. This setting specifically controls the sharing of records in customer or partner communities. It’s different from the internal OWD setting, which affects internal Salesforce users (e.g., employees). Once set to Private, you can configure additional sharing rules if needed, such as owner-based sharing rules, to provide community users with access to their own Account records. Why the other options are incorrect: Create an account record type for external accounts: While creating record types might be useful for segmenting different types of Accounts, it doesn't directly address the issue of controlling visibility of Account records. Record types primarily help control page layouts and business processes, not sharing and access. Define an owner-based sharing rule for external accounts: While you can define owner-based sharing rules, changing the External OWD to Private is a more direct and effective way to control visibility. After setting the OWD to Private, you can define sharing rules if necessary, but the OWD setting should be the first step. Define a permission set for external accounts: A permission set can be used to grant additional permissions or restrict access to specific fields or features but does not address the issue of record-level access to Account records. The OWD setting is what determines the visibility of records in the first place.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) increased its Salesforce development efforts so That it now has multiple custom development efforts happening in parallel. CK's developers and admins perform the customizations and have Complained that working in one sandbox has led to many problems. They Requested a solution in which they can work in at least 20 different Sandboxes at once, that all start with the same base configuration and Dat What should an app builder use to solve the problem?
sourceExplanation: The correct answer is: Partial Copy Sandboxes. Explanation: Cloud Kicks (CK) is facing challenges because multiple custom development efforts are happening simultaneously in a single sandbox, causing issues like conflicts or configuration inconsistencies. The team needs a solution that enables them to work in at least 20 different sandboxes with the same base configuration and data. Partial Copy Sandboxes are the ideal solution in this case. Here's why: Partial Copy Sandboxes provide a way to create multiple sandboxes with a subset of your production data. This is particularly useful when you need sandboxes that are lighter in terms of data storage (compared to Full Copy sandboxes) but still contain realistic sample data from your production org for testing and development. You can clone the same base configuration into multiple sandboxes (up to 20 in this case) and ensure that each of them starts with the same data set and metadata configuration, making it easy for multiple teams to work in parallel without stepping on each other's toes. Partial Copy Sandboxes include: All metadata (like custom objects, fields, etc.) A subset of production data (usually 5GB of data, but you can configure the data selection to match your needs) This setup will allow CK’s developers and admins to work independently in separate environments while still having the same base data and configuration across multiple sandboxes. Why the other options are incorrect: Sandbox Cloning: While cloning a sandbox creates an identical copy of an existing sandbox, it does not provide the ability to create multiple sandboxes simultaneously with a common base configuration. Cloning helps you copy a single sandbox, but it doesn’t help you scale to 20 distinct sandboxes for parallel work. Full Copy Sandboxes: Full Copy Sandboxes include all of the production data, but they can be more expensive and slower to create because they carry over all of your production data. These are ideal when you need a full replica of your production environment, but for this scenario, where you need multiple sandboxes with only relevant subsets of data, Partial Copy Sandboxes are more appropriate and resource-efficient. Sandbox Refreshes: A sandbox refresh allows you to refresh an existing sandbox with a new copy of your production data, but it does not solve the issue of needing multiple, independent sandboxes at once. Refreshing a sandbox would overwrite its existing configuration and data, which is not the solution when you want multiple environments to start with the same base configuration but continue independently.

stem: An app builder wants to limit the amount of fields users see When creating a new Opportunity. Once they fill out the required fields and Save, the full record page with additional fields relevant to the Opportunity Type becomes available. How could this be accomplished?

options.text: Make the Opportunity type a required field on the initial Opportunity page layout and Use automation to update the record type based on the Opportunity type.
Use different page layouts for Opportunity types based on the user profile.
Once the required fields are populated, use a sharing rule to share the new fields with The user.
Hide additional sections on the page layout and the users how to manually Expand them when they want to fill in the fields in the hidden sections.

sourceExplanation: Explanation: This approach ensures that the users can initially create an Opportunity with only the required fields visible. The process involves the following steps: Required Field: By making the Opportunity Type a required field on the initial page layout, you ensure that users must select the Opportunity Type when they first create the record. This ensures that the relevant Opportunity Type is set right away. Automation: After the record is saved, you can use automation such as a Record-Triggered Flow or a Process Builder to automatically update the record type based on the Opportunity Type selected. This enables a more customized page layout for the specific Opportunity Type, showing additional fields relevant to that type. This solution optimizes the user experience by initially showing only the essential fields and then dynamically adjusting the record layout based on the Opportunity Type, ensuring that users see only the most relevant fields at each stage. Why the other options are incorrect: Use different page layouts for Opportunity types based on the user profile: While using different page layouts is a valid option, this solution requires maintaining multiple layouts, which can complicate the process, especially if you need to maintain a consistent user experience across various Opportunity Types. Additionally, this doesn't directly address the requirement of limiting the fields when the Opportunity is created. Once the required fields are populated, use a sharing rule to share the new fields with the user: Sharing rules are used for record-level access, not field-level visibility. They control access to records but not the fields visible on those records. Therefore, this would not solve the problem of limiting the visible fields during Opportunity creation. Hide additional sections on the page layout and the users how to manually expand them when they want to fill in the fields in the hidden sections: Hiding sections manually and asking users to expand them is not an optimal solution. It adds complexity to the user experience and might lead to inconsistent data entry. The goal is to make the process smooth and intuitive, so the automation-based approach is a better fit.

stem: At Universal Containers, the VP of Service has requested a visual indicator flag on each case, based On the case priority. High-priority cases should be flagged red, medium-priority should be flagged Yellow, and low-priority cases should be flagged green. Which two formulas will accomplish this requirement?
sourceExplanation: Explanation: Option A: The IMAGE() function is used to display an image on the page. The CASE() function checks the value of the Priority field and returns the corresponding image URL based on the priority level. If the Priority is "Low," it will display the green flag, "Medium" will show the yellow flag, and "High" will show the red flag. If no priority matches, it defaults to showing an empty image (/s.gif). Option C: This formula uses the CASE() function to check the Priority field and return the respective image URLs. Similar to Option A, it displays the green, yellow, or red flag based on the priority, and defaults to a blank image (/s.gif) if the Priority is not one of the specified values. Why the other options are incorrect: Option B: The formula works, but it is unnecessarily complex. While it does check for the "Low," "Medium," and "High" priorities and returns the appropriate image, it uses multiple nested IF() statements instead of the simpler and more readable CASE() function, which is preferred for this type of logic. Also, it has a minor syntax issue where the closing quotation marks and parentheses are misplaced for the "Medium" image path. Option D: This formula uses nested IF() statements wrapped in an IMAGE() function, which will work but is less clean and readable than using the CASE() function. Also, it has the same syntax issues as Option B, particularly with misplaced quotation marks and parentheses. It would likely result in an error or incorrect behavior due to incorrect formatting.

stem: An app builder at Universal Containers has been asked to add The Chatter feed to a custom object record page. Which approach should the app builder use?

options.text: Add a custom Chatter feed component.
Add the standard related list component
Add the standard Chatter feed component.
Add the Chatter feed component from the AppExchange.

sourceExplanation: Explanation: In Salesforce, to display the Chatter feed on a custom object record page, you should use the standard Chatter Feed component. This is a pre-built component provided by Salesforce that you can add directly to any Lightning page layout for custom objects, accounts, opportunities, and other Salesforce standard or custom objects. By adding the standard Chatter feed component, users will be able to see and interact with Chatter posts, comments, and mentions related to that specific record. Why the other options are incorrect: Add a custom Chatter feed component: Salesforce does not require or recommend creating a custom Chatter feed component for this purpose. The standard Chatter feed component is already available and is designed for this use case. Add the standard related list component: The related list component displays related records, but it doesn't specifically show the Chatter feed. stem: The brokers at DreamHouse Realty (DR) are having an issue When using the Salesforce mobile app on their iPhones. There are several Key fields on the contact record they need access to at a glance. Because Of the small screen, they currently have to scroll down the page to view the Information. What should the app builder at DR use to configure the Salesforce mobile App to these key fields at the top of the screen?
sourceExplanation: The correct solution is to use a Compact Layout. Compact layouts allow you to control which fields are displayed in the highlights section of a record, providing a condensed view of key information at the top of the page. This is especially useful on mobile devices, where screen real estate is limited. By setting up a compact layout, the brokers at DreamHouse Realty will be able to see the most important fields without having to scroll down the page. Why the other options are incorrect: Mobile navigation: Mobile navigation controls the structure and flow of the app’s tabs and pages, but it doesn't allow you to customize which fields appear on a record page. It’s useful for overall app navigation, not for field layout. Record Detail component: The Record Detail component displays all fields on a record page, but it does not allow you to prioritize key fields to be displayed at the top of the screen. It shows a comprehensive view, which would still require scrolling on mobile devices. Object-specific action: Object-specific actions are used to create or update records directly from the mobile app, but they don't affect the layout of the record detail page itself. They would help with creating or updating contacts but won't address the issue of field visibility on the record page.

stem: A sales rep at AW Computing is unable to find what they are looking for While scrolling through their Chatter fee How can a filter be utilized to only posts from their key account and Opportunity records?
sourceExplanation: The correct solution is to Create a Chatter stream. A Chatter stream allows users to filter and follow posts related to specific records, such as key accounts and Opportunity records. By creating a Chatter stream, the sales rep can focus on the updates and discussions that are most relevant to them, without having to sift through unrelated posts in the Chatter feed. Why the other options are incorrect: Create Chatter bookmarks: Chatter bookmarks allow users to save specific posts or discussions for quick reference, but they do not offer a way to filter or focus on posts from specific records like key accounts or opportunities. They are more for saving specific content, not for filtering or streamlining the feed. Create a Chatter notification: Chatter notifications alert users about updates, mentions, or replies, but they don't provide a way to filter posts in the feed itself. Notifications are useful for keeping track of new activity, but they don't organize or filter Chatter content based on specific records. Create a Chatter group: Chatter groups are good for creating collaborative spaces for teams or specific topics. However, they don’t automatically filter content from specific records like key accounts or opportunities in the general Chatter feed. Groups are a broader communication tool rather than a focused filtering solution.

stem: Which two features can be used to allow users to access Flows?
sourceExplanation: The two features that can be used to allow users to access Flows are: Flow Launcher: The Flow Launcher is a feature specifically designed to make it easy for users to launch and run flows directly from the user interface. It provides a streamlined experience for accessing and starting a flow, making it more convenient for users to engage with business processes without needing to navigate through complex menus or setups. Quick Action: A Quick Action allows users to launch flows directly from record pages, the Salesforce mobile app, or even custom buttons. By creating a Quick Action, an app builder can add a flow to a record’s page layout, enabling users to start the flow with just a click or tap. This is one of the most common and effective ways to integrate flows into Salesforce user interfaces. Why the other options are incorrect: Apex: Apex is Salesforce’s programming language, used to write custom logic and processes. While you can call a flow from Apex, Apex itself is not a direct method for users to access or interact with flows. It’s more of a backend tool for developers. Approval Process: An Approval Process is a predefined workflow used to automate approval steps for records. Although it might involve flows as part of its actions, the Approval Process itself doesn't directly provide a way for users to initiate or access flows.

stem: Which two places can an app builder go to see a list of available Custom Lightning Components in their org?
sourceExplanation: The two places where an app builder can go to see a list of available Custom Lightning Components in their org are: Lightning App Builder: The Lightning App Builder is the primary tool for creating and customizing Lightning pages. It allows app builders to drag and drop Lightning components (both standard and custom) onto the page. To view custom components that have been created in the org, you can open the Lightning App Builder and see the list of available components in the component palette. Lightning Components in Setup: The Lightning Components section in Setup provides a centralized view of all Lightning components in your org, including custom components. This is where you can manage, configure, and deploy Lightning components that have been developed in your org. Why the other options are incorrect: Visualforce components in Setup: This section in Setup is used to manage Visualforce pages, not Lightning components. While you can see custom Visualforce pages here, it won't show you any custom Lightning components, which are separate from Visualforce. Salesforce Optimizer App: The Salesforce Optimizer App is a tool that provides recommendations on how to improve your Salesforce org’s performance, but it does not directly show a list of available custom Lightning components. It's more about analyzing your org and offering suggestions for optimization.

stem: Nickname _ c is a custom text field on a contact record that is Utilized to override the contact name appearing on an email template. This Field is not required and is not always filled in. Which formula should an app builder use to select the contact's preferred Name for email communications?
sourceExplanation: The correct formula is: IF (NOT (ISBLANK (Nickname_c)), Nickname_c, FirstName) This formula checks if the Nickname_c field is blank. If Nickname_c has a value, it will use that value (the custom nickname) as the preferred name for email communications. If Nickname_c is blank, it will fall back to the FirstName field. Breakdown of the formula: ISBLANK (Nickname_c): This function checks if the Nickname_c field is empty or not. NOT (ISBLANK (Nickname_c)): The NOT function reverses the result of ISBLANK. So, it returns TRUE if Nickname_c is not blank (i.e., it has a value). Nickname_c: If the Nickname_c field is not blank, the formula returns the value of Nickname_c. FirstName: If Nickname_c is blank, the formula defaults to using the FirstName. Why the other options are incorrect: IF (NOT (BLANKVALUE (Nickname_c)), Nickname_c, FirstName): The BLANKVALUE() function is used to check if a field is blank and return a default value if true. However, in this case, ISBLANK() is a better fit to check for blank fields, and BLANKVALUE() would not work exactly as intended when checking if a field is specifically not blank. IF(ISNULL(Nickname_c), Nickname_c, FirstName): The ISNULL() function checks for a null value, but Nickname_c is a custom text field, and text fields are never null—they are either blank or contain text. So, using ISNULL() is not suitable for checking blank text fields. IF (TEXT (Nickname_c), Nickname_c, FirstName): The TEXT() function is used to convert a value to text, but it's not needed in this case, as Nickname_c is already a text field. This formula would cause an issue since TEXT() does not check if a value is blank or not.

stem: An app builder at Cloud Kicks has been working on changes to a Custom Shoe Sales app in a sandbox and is ready to deploy their changes To production with a change set. Part of the work included updates to a Permission set. What should the app builder take into consideration when deploying the Change set to production?

options.text: The existing permission set will be completely overwritten.
The deployed permission set will only contain changes related to the change set.
Changes to field-level security in the permission set will not be applied.
The deployed permission set will merge with the existing permission set.

sourceExplanation: The correct answer is: The deployed permission set will only contain changes related to the change set. Here's why: When you deploy a Permission Set via a change set, only the changes included in the change set will be deployed to production. Any settings in the permission set that are not part of the change set will remain as they were in the production org. Detailed Breakdown: The deployed permission set will only contain changes related to the change set: This is the correct behavior. When deploying a permission set through a change set, only the specific changes that you’ve included in the change set will be transferred to the target org. Any existing settings or permissions that were not modified in the sandbox will remain intact in the production org. This allows you to deploy just the updates, without overwriting or disrupting other settings. Why the other options are incorrect: The existing permission set will be completely overwritten: This is incorrect. A permission set deployed via a change set does not overwrite the entire permission set in the target org. It only applies the changes that are included in the change set. Unchanged settings will not be affected. Changes to field-level security in the permission set will not be applied: This is also incorrect. Field-level security changes included in the change set will be applied when deploying the permission set. Field-level security settings are part of the permission set and are deployed when included in the change set. The deployed permission set will merge with the existing permission set: This is not correct either. The changes in the permission set will not merge with the existing permission set. Instead, the permission set in the target org will reflect only the modifications in the change set. Existing settings that were not part of the change set will remain unchanged.

stem: A business user wants a quick way to edit a record's status and enter a Custom due date field from the record's feed in Salesforce Mobile App. What should be used to accomplish this?
sourceExplanation: The correct solution is to use a Custom Action. Here's why: Custom Action: Custom Actions allow you to create a quick and intuitive way for users to interact with records. For a mobile user, a custom action can be added directly in the record's feed to provide fast access to update fields like a record's status and due date. Custom actions can be configured to allow users to update fields, create records, or invoke flows from within the record page, making it ideal for this scenario. How it works: You can create a Custom Action to specifically update fields like Status and Due Date for the record. This action can then be placed directly within the record feed in Salesforce Mobile, enabling the business user to quickly edit the record’s status and due date without navigating away from the page. Why the other options are incorrect: Custom quick access link: Quick access links are used to provide shortcuts to specific pages or URLs but do not directly allow users to edit or update fields. They are not suitable for updating fields like status and due date directly in the feed. Custom button: Custom buttons are often used in Salesforce Classic or for invoking actions like redirecting to a specific page, but they do not easily integrate into Salesforce mobile feeds or provide a streamlined way to update fields directly in the record’s feed. Custom URL formula field: A Custom URL formula field creates clickable links that navigate to a URL but doesn’t facilitate field updates directly in the record. It also doesn't offer the interactive flexibility needed to update fields like status and due date from the feed in the mobile app.

stem: Dream House Realty is building a custom Lightning app to track its expanding solar water Collection business. The Lightning app currently contains a custom Lightning record page with Standard components. From which two resources should an app builder get custom components to bring into the new Lightning app?
sourceExplanation: The two resources from which an app builder should get custom components to bring into the new Lightning app are: Lightning Components: Lightning Components are custom components built specifically for use within the Lightning Experience. These can be custom-built components using Aura or LWC (Lightning Web Components). An app builder can either create new components in the org or reuse existing components. Once built, these components can be added to the custom Lightning record page to enhance the app's functionality. AppExchange: AppExchange is Salesforce's marketplace where users can find pre-built solutions and components developed by Salesforce partners or the community. Many custom Lightning components are available on AppExchange that can be installed and used in your Lightning apps. These components often solve common business needs or extend Salesforce's standard functionality. Why the other options are incorrect: Import Wizard: The Import Wizard is used to import data (like leads, accounts, contacts, etc.) into Salesforce but does not have anything to do with custom components. It’s not a resource for adding custom components to a Lightning app. Apex Code: Apex Code is used for server-side logic, and while it can be used to handle more complex operations or logic for Lightning components, Apex itself isn't a source of components to add to the app. However, you may use Apex in conjunction with Lightning components to build functionality, but Apex isn't a direct resource for adding UI components to a Lightning page.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) utilizes two custom picklist fields Called sales_Organization_c and Pricing_Tier _ Which validation rule should an app builder use to ensure Pricing Tier_c is required for customers with a Sales Organization_c value of Canada?
sourceExplanation: The correct validation rule to ensure that Pricing_Tier_c is required for customers with a Sales_Organization_c value of "Canada" is: AND(ISPICKVAL(Sales_Organization_c, 'Canada'), ISBLANK(TEXT(Pricing_Tier_c))) Breakdown: ISPICKVAL(Sales_Organization_c, 'Canada'): This checks if the Sales_Organization_c picklist field is set to "Canada." ISBLANK(TEXT(Pricing_Tier_c)): This checks if the Pricing_Tier_c picklist field is blank. Since picklist fields cannot be directly checked for "blank" values, we convert it to text using TEXT() and then use ISBLANK() to check if it's empty. The AND() function ensures that the validation rule only fires when both conditions are true: The Sales_Organization_c field is "Canada." The Pricing_Tier_c field is blank (not selected). Why the other options are incorrect: ISPICKVAL(Sales_Organization_c, 'Canada') & ISNULL(Pricing_Tier_c): ISNULL() is not appropriate for picklist fields. Use ISBLANK(TEXT(...)) for picklists. Additionally, & is incorrect here; AND() should be used to combine the conditions. IF(ISNULL(Sales_Organization_c='Canada', ISBLANK(TEXT(Pricing_Tier_c)), TRUE): The syntax here is incorrect. The IF() function isn't correctly structured. Also, ISNULL() does not apply to picklist fields, and the logic is malformed. OR(ISPICKVAL(Sales_Organization_c, 'Canada'), ISBLANK(TEXT(Pricing_Tier_c))): The OR() function would fire if either condition is true. We need both conditions to be true (Sales Organization is "Canada" and Pricing Tier is blank), so AND() should be used instead of OR().

stem: The Dream House Realty (DR) service manager asks for some Improvements in case management. They want to enforce compliance so That cases are unable to be reverted to an earlier case status, and to Ensure that certain fields are required when specific case criteria are met. Which solution should an app builder implement to meet these Requirements?
sourceExplanation: The correct solution is Validation Rules. Here's why: Validation Rules are the most appropriate solution for enforcing business rules, such as preventing a case from being reverted to an earlier status and ensuring that certain fields are required based on specific case criteria. Preventing case status reversion: You can use a validation rule to prevent users from changing the case status back to a previous value (e.g., ensuring a case can’t be reverted from "Closed" back to "In Progress"). This can be done by checking the current case status against the previous value and throwing an error if an invalid status change is attempted. Enforcing field requirements based on case criteria: You can also use validation rules to make certain fields required when specific case conditions are met (e.g., making fields like "Resolution" or "Priority" required when a case is marked as "High Priority"). Why the other options are incorrect: Approval Process: Approval processes are used for automating the approval of records (such as opportunities, quotes, or cases) based on certain criteria, but they aren't designed to enforce restrictions like preventing status changes or making fields required based on criteria. Approval processes also do not provide real-time enforcement of data quality during the creation or editing of cases. Dependent Picklist: Dependent picklists are used to control the values available in one picklist field based on the value selected in another picklist field. While they are useful for narrowing down options and enforcing logical relationships between fields, they don't address the requirement of preventing status changes or ensuring fields are required based on case criteria. Case Flow: Case Flows are used for guiding users through complex processes, often involving multiple steps or fields, but they don't directly enforce business rules like preventing status reversion or requiring fields based on case criteria. Flows are more focused on process automation, and although they can ensure certain fields are filled in, they are not typically used to enforce restrictions on record changes like validation rules.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) wants to delete data in several fields for 5,000 Lead records. UC exported the selected record Ids and fields that need to have data deleted in a CSV file. Which two steps should an app builder suggest to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Import Wizard to update leads using the CSV file.
Use Data Loader to update leads using the CSV file.
Select Insert Null Values in Settings.

sourceExplanation: The two steps the app builder should suggest to meet the requirements of deleting data in several fields for 5,000 Lead records are: Use Data Loader to update leads using the CSV file. Data Loader is the correct tool for updating large volumes of records, such as 5,000 Leads. It can be used to clear (delete) data in specific fields by setting those fields to null in the CSV file. This is an efficient way to delete data for a large number of records at once. When using Data Loader, you can choose Update operation and include a CSV file with the Lead IDs and the fields that need to be cleared. Note: In the CSV file, you should include the record IDs of the Leads and leave the columns for the fields you want to delete blank (or set to null if applicable). Select Insert Null Values in Settings. When using Data Loader to update the records and clear data, you need to enable the "Insert Null Values" setting in the Data Loader’s settings. This ensures that if a field is left blank or has a null value in the CSV file, Data Loader will update the record and remove the value from that field, effectively deleting the data. Why the other options are incorrect: Select the correct record type. Record type selection is important when you're dealing with different page layouts or business processes, but it doesn't directly relate to the process of deleting data from fields. Since you're already specifying the Lead records with their IDs in the CSV file, the record type selection is not relevant in this case. Use Import Wizard to update leads using the CSV file. The Import Wizard is a great tool for importing records, but it is limited in its ability to handle complex operations like updating existing records and clearing data. The Import Wizard cannot handle null values in the same way Data Loader can, and for mass deletion of data, Data Loader is a better fit.

stem: A recently refreshed partial sandbox at Cloud Kicks has no data in The custom object Shipping. Checking in production, there are two million Rows of data in the object. What could be the reason the data is missing?

options.text: The sandbox was refreshed too early.
The sandbox is still populating dat
The selected objects in the sandbox template.
The partial sandbox is at capacity.

sourceExplanation: When a partial sandbox is refreshed, Salesforce allows you to choose specific objects to include in the sandbox. If an object is not selected in the sandbox template during the refresh, its data will not be copied into the sandbox. This would explain why the Shipping object data, even though present in production, is missing in the sandbox. In partial sandboxes, only a portion of the production data is replicated, typically up to 5 GB. The objects you select for the sandbox template will have their data transferred over, while others will be excluded. Therefore, it’s important to ensure that all the necessary objects are included in the template to get the relevant data. Why the other options are incorrect: The sandbox was refreshed too early: If this were the case, the sandbox refresh would likely fail or be incomplete, not just miss data for one object. The sandbox is still populating data: This would typically apply to the initial creation of a sandbox or if there were issues, but after the refresh, the data should be available almost immediately. The partial sandbox is at capacity: If the sandbox had reached its data capacity, it would have generated an error during the refresh, preventing it from completing. It would not selectively exclude data for a specific object.

stem: Cloud Kicks recently implemented the application lifecycle Management process to its release management strategy. Which category handles bug fixes and simple changes?
sourceExplanation: In the context of Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) and release management, the category that handles bug fixes and simple changes is typically referred to as a Patch release. Patch releases focus on addressing small fixes, such as bug fixes, minor enhancements, and patches that don't involve significant changes to functionality or require extensive testing. These are quick updates aimed at resolving issues that don't drastically alter the system's core features or architecture. Why the other options are incorrect: Roll: This is not typically a recognized release category in standard release management processes. It might refer to specific deployment strategies in certain contexts, but it's not commonly used to categorize types of releases. Major: Major releases involve significant changes or new features. These types of releases might introduce new functionality, large-scale changes, or updates that could impact the system's architecture and require substantial testing. Minor: Minor releases are typically used for adding features or making improvements that are not as large as a major release. They might introduce new functionality but still remain within the broader framework of the existing system. Unlike a patch, they often involve more extensive changes.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to initiate an automatic daily up of its Salesforce org. Which tool should an app builder recommend for this task?
sourceExplanation: The correct tool for initiating an automatic daily backup of Salesforce data is the Data Export Service. The Data Export Service in Salesforce allows users to schedule regular, automated backups of their Salesforce data. By using this tool, Northern Trail Outfitters can set up an automatic daily export of data, including all objects (standard and custom) and related data. The export files can be downloaded as .zip files containing CSV files for each object, and these can be saved locally or to an external storage location. Why the other options are incorrect: Refresh full copy sandbox: While full copy sandboxes can be used to create an exact replica of the production environment, including both data and metadata, it's not specifically intended for regular automated backups. Refreshing a full sandbox typically requires manual intervention and is done periodically, not on a daily schedule. Additionally, sandboxes are primarily for testing and development purposes, not for routine data backups. AppExchange package: The AppExchange offers various tools and apps that can enhance Salesforce functionality, but it's not a built-in tool for automatic daily backups. While some AppExchange packages might offer backup features, the Data Export Service is the built-in solution specifically designed for this task. Report export: Report exports are useful for extracting data from Salesforce in a report format, but they are not designed for full, automated, daily backups of all Salesforce data. Reports can only export the data included in a report, not the entire set of data across all objects in your Salesforce org.

stem: Universal Containers deployed an app in a large change set from a Developer Sandbox to a Developer Pro Sandbox used for testing. After Testing, changes had to be made to several of the components in the Change set. How should an app builder move the new changes to the Developer Pro Sandbox?

options.text: Rename the change set, add the changes and re-deploy.
Clone the change set and re-deploy.
Refresh the test sandbox and re-deploy the change set.
Update the change set and re-deploy.

sourceExplanation: The correct solution is to Clone the change set and re-deploy. When working with change sets in Salesforce, you cannot edit or update an already deployed change set directly. Once a change set is deployed, it becomes immutable (i.e., it can't be modified). Therefore, if changes need to be made after a change set has already been deployed (such as in this case where updates were needed after testing), the app builder should: Clone the change set: This creates a copy of the original change set with the same components, allowing you to keep track of what was originally included. Make the necessary changes: Add the new or modified components to the cloned change set. Re-deploy: Deploy the updated change set to the Developer Pro Sandbox again. Why the other options are incorrect: Rename the change set, add the changes, and re-deploy: You cannot rename a change set to modify its contents after it has been deployed. Once a change set is deployed, it can't be modified. You would need to create a new change set (via cloning) to deploy any changes. Refresh the test sandbox and re-deploy the change set: Refreshing the sandbox will erase all custom data, configurations, and metadata in the sandbox, effectively resetting it. While this will give you a clean test environment, it doesn't address the issue of modifying or adding components to an already-deployed change set. You'd still need to create and deploy a new change set for any updates. Update the change set and re-deploy: As mentioned earlier, change sets cannot be updated once deployed. The only option for re-deploying new or modified components is to clone the change set and modify that clone.

stem: An app builder just added a lookup field to Account from the Existing custom object, Box. Which report type is automatically created?
sourceExplanation: The correct report type automatically created when an app builder adds a lookup field to Account from the existing custom object Box is: Accounts with Boxes Why this is the correct answer: Lookup relationships create a link between two objects, where one object (in this case, the Box object) references another (the Account object). When a lookup field is added to an object (here, Box), Salesforce automatically generates a "with" report type. This is because Salesforce assumes that you'll likely want to view the records in the primary object (Accounts) with the related records from the secondary object (Box). So, by creating a lookup field on Box that links to Account, Salesforce will automatically create the "Accounts with Boxes" report type. This type allows you to view Accounts and the associated Boxes. Why the other options are incorrect: Boxes with Accounts: This would typically be used if the lookup relationship were on the Account object referencing Box, but in your case, the lookup field was added to the Box object. So, this type is not automatically created. Boxes with or without Accounts: This report type would include all Box records, even those that don't have an associated Account. While useful, it's not the default report type automatically created in this scenario. It's more typical for this to be a custom report type. Accounts with or without Boxes: This type would be useful if you wanted to see all Accounts, whether or not they have a Box associated. However, the automatic report type created by Salesforce in this case will only link Accounts to Boxes, not necessarily show Accounts without Boxes.

stem: The app builder at Cloud Kicks has created a custom object named Delivery_c to track the Details of products shipped to customers. Which two actions should the app builder take to prevent users in the shipping department from Deleting delivery records?

options.text: Remove the delete button from the Delivery page layout.
Use a permission set to remove the Delete permission.
Remove the Delete permission from the Shipper profile.
Change the organization-wide default of deliveries to Private.

sourceExplanation: To prevent users in the shipping department from deleting delivery records in Salesforce, the app builder should take the following two actions: Remove the Delete button from the Delivery page layout. Removing the Delete button from the Delivery object's page layout ensures that users in the shipping department cannot easily delete records from the UI. This action hides the button, but it doesn't remove the delete permission completely from users who may have the necessary permissions to delete records via other means (e.g., API or data import). However, this is a good first step to restrict accidental deletions via the UI. Use a permission set to remove the Delete permission. By using a Permission Set to specifically remove the Delete permission for the Delivery object, you ensure that users cannot delete records even if they have access to the object. This method allows for more granular control over who can delete records, as permission sets are applied on top of the user's existing profile permissions. Why the other options are incorrect: Remove the Delete permission from the Shipper profile. This action will also work to prevent the users with the Shipper profile from deleting Delivery records. However, if there are multiple user profiles in the shipping department, the app builder would have to make this change to each relevant profile. This method is more rigid and less flexible than using a permission set. A Permission Set allows for easier updates and is often preferred for controlling specific permissions like Delete on an object. Change the organization-wide default of deliveries to Private. Changing the organization-wide default (OWD) for the Delivery object to Private would control record visibility, but it does not directly affect delete permissions. Users could still delete records they have access to, so while it might help in controlling who can see the records, it doesn't necessarily prevent deletions. This is more relevant to controlling visibility, not actions like delete.

stem: DreamHouse Realty wants to import its property records from an external system into Salesforce. The app builder will use an external ID field to house the property ID from the external System. Which two field types are allowed as an external ID?
sourceExplanation: The two field types that can be used as external ID fields in Salesforce are: Text field: Text fields can be used as external IDs. An external ID is often a unique identifier from an external system, and since these IDs are typically alphanumeric (such as property IDs or reference numbers), a Text field is commonly used. Number field: Number fields can also be used as external IDs, especially when the external system uses numeric IDs (e.g., product IDs, invoice numbers, etc.). Since external IDs must be unique for each record, a Number field can serve as a valid external ID as long as the values are unique across records. Why the other options are incorrect: Phone field: A Phone field cannot be used as an external ID. Although phone numbers may be unique in some systems, Salesforce does not support using phone fields as external IDs for data import or integration purposes. URL field: A URL field also cannot be used as an external ID. While URLs may be unique, Salesforce does not support URL fields as external IDs for the purpose of matching or importing records.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) has created the custom objects Trail and Park in Salesforce to track trails and parks respectively. NTO wants to Track the total number of trails a park has on the park record without writing any code. Which two actions should an app builder take to accomplish this requirement?

options.text: Use a formula field on the Park record to the total number of trails.
–Use a roll-up summary field on the Park record to the total number of Trails.
Use a master-detail relationship between the Park and Trail objects.
Use a lookup relationship between the Park and Trail objects.

sourceExplanation: To track the total number of trails associated with each Park record in Salesforce, without writing any code, the app builder should use the following two actions: Use a roll-up summary field on the Park record to the total number of Trails: Roll-up summary fields are designed to calculate values from related records in a master-detail relationship. Since the app builder wants to track the total number of Trail records associated with each Park, a roll-up summary field can be created on the Park object to automatically count the number of related Trail records. This is the best solution for summarizing the data without the need for code. Use a master-detail relationship between the Park and Trail objects: In order for a roll-up summary field to work, there must be a master-detail relationship between the two objects. A master-detail relationship ensures that the Trail records are tightly associated with the Park records. In this case, the Park would be the master, and the Trail would be the detail, allowing you to use a roll-up summary field to calculate the number of related Trail records. Why the other options are incorrect: Use a formula field on the Park record to the total number of trails: A formula field can calculate values based on other fields, but it cannot aggregate data from related records. For example, a formula field cannot automatically count the number of related Trail records on the Park object. Roll-up summary fields are specifically designed for this kind of aggregation. Use a lookup relationship between the Park and Trail objects: While a lookup relationship allows for linking records between objects, it does not support the use of roll-up summary fields. Roll-up summary fields only work in master-detail relationships, so a lookup relationship would not allow the app builder to use the roll-up summary field to count the number of related Trail records on the Park record.

stem: DreamHouse Realty (DR) asks for some improvements in case management. They want to enforce process compliance so that cases are unable to be reverted to an earlier case status, and to ensure that certain fields are required when specific case criteria are met. Which solution should an app builder implement to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure validation rules with help text.
Create dependent picklist fields and set them as require
Make the fields required on the page layout.
Use an approval process to check field criteria are met.

sourceExplanation: The correct solution to meet DreamHouse Realty's requirements of enforcing process compliance in case management is to configure validation rules with help text. Here's why: Validation Rules are used to enforce business logic in Salesforce by preventing users from saving records if they do not meet certain criteria. In this scenario: Preventing cases from being reverted to an earlier case status can be achieved by creating a validation rule that checks the current and previous status of the case and ensures that users cannot change the status to an earlier value. Ensuring that certain fields are required based on specific case criteria can also be done with a validation rule. For example, if a case is marked as "High Priority," you can make certain fields required (like a resolution or root cause) based on the case's status or type. Help text within the validation rule can be added to guide users on why a specific field is required or why a status change is not allowed. Why the other options are incorrect: Create dependent picklist fields and set them as required: Dependent picklists are useful when you want the value of one picklist field to control the available values in another picklist. However, they are not designed to enforce rules around case status changes or make fields required based on case criteria. Dependent picklists control field value relationships, not business process enforcement like validation rules. Make the fields required on the page layout: Making fields required on the page layout ensures users cannot leave those fields blank when creating or editing a record. However, this does not enforce business logic (like preventing a case status change). It also does not allow conditional field requirements based on specific criteria (e.g., requiring fields only when certain case conditions are met). Validation rules, on the other hand, can provide these dynamic, conditional requirements. Use an approval process to check field criteria are met: Approval processes are designed to automate the approval of records based on criteria and can be used for cases, but they are not meant to enforce field requirements during case creation or editing. Approval processes are primarily for workflows that require managerial approval, not for controlling data entry during regular case updates.

stem: DreamHouse Realty (DR) is expanding into subsidised housing by partnering with local government entities. DR uses Sales Cloud and has enabled field history tracking on the Opportunity object. Due to increased information requirements, the App Dev team is changing Text Area (Long) fields to Rich Text fields to allow for up to 1,000 characters and better descriptions. Which two considerations should be made by the team?

options.text: Field History Tracking records value changes of 255 characters or less.
Rich text field values of all lengths are displayed fully in reports.
Data loss may occur when changing custom field types.
Audit Trail is available through REST API extracts.

sourceExplanation: Field History Tracking records value changes of 255 characters or less is a correct consideration because Salesforce only stores and displays the first 255 characters of a field change in Field History Tracking, even if the field itself supports longer values such as Rich Text fields. Data loss may occur when changing custom field types is also a correct consideration. When converting a Text Area (Long) field to a Rich Text field, existing data can be affected, especially if formatting or unsupported content is introduced. The App Dev team should validate data carefully before making the change. Why the other options are incorrect: Rich text field values of all lengths are displayed fully in reports: This is incorrect because reports do not display the full rich text formatting or unlimited character content. Rich Text fields are often truncated or displayed as plain text in reports. Audit Trail is available through REST API extracts: This is incorrect because Field History Tracking data is not considered an audit trail and is not fully accessible as a formal audit log through REST API extracts.

stem: Ursa Major Solar is ramping up the sales team to meet increased demand. As part of the short ramp up for these new reps, the manager wants to provide a help guide to enable reps to easily get help where needed during the different sales processes. Which solution should an app builder recommend?
sourceExplanation: Path is the correct solution because it provides on-screen guidance for users at each stage of a sales process. It allows admins to display key fields, tips, and helpful information directly on the record, enabling new sales reps to get contextual help as they move through different stages. Why the other options are incorrect: Chatter Publisher: Chatter Publisher is used to post updates, polls, or files but does not guide users through sales processes or provide structured help. Journey Builder: Journey Builder is a Marketing Cloud tool used for customer journeys and is not designed to support sales rep guidance in Sales Cloud. Flow: Flow is used to automate business processes but does not provide inline guidance or help content tied to sales stages.

stem: An app builder has a custom component they want to make available on the utility bar, but the component is unavailable. How should the component be tagged?

options.text: For use on the utility bar.
For use in Lightning App Builder.

sourceExplanation: For use on the utility bar is the correct answer because a custom Lightning component must be explicitly tagged to be available for placement in the Utility Bar. Without this designation, the component will not appear as an option when configuring the utility bar in App Manager. Why the other options are incorrect: For use on record pages: This tag makes the component available for Lightning record pages, not for the utility bar. For use in Lightning App Builder: This is a general designation that allows components to appear in the App Builder but does not specifically enable use in the utility bar. For use in App Manager: App Manager is used to configure apps, including the utility bar, but tagging a component for App Manager alone does not make it eligible for placement in the utility bar.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to set up a new opportunity approval process and execute various action items based on the initial submission. Which three action types should an app builder use in the approval process?
sourceExplanation: Email Alert is a correct action type because approval processes can send automated email notifications when an approval request is submitted, approved, rejected, or recalled. Task is a correct action type because approval processes can automatically create tasks to assign follow-up work to users during different stages of the approval lifecycle. Outbound Message is a correct action type because approval processes can send SOAP messages to external systems to notify or trigger actions outside of Salesforce. Why the other options are incorrect: Invocable Flow: Invocable Flows cannot be directly executed as approval process actions. Approval processes have a fixed set of supported actions. Decision Element: Decision elements are used within Flow logic and are not available as action types in approval processes.

stem: An app builder is creating a custom object called Testimonial__c and wants to connect Testimonial__c records with both the submitter's Contact record and Account record. If the Account is deleted, the Testimonial__c records should also be deleted. If the Contact is deleted, but the Account remains, the Testimonial__c records should remain. How should this be accomplished?

options.text: Create a master-detail relationship from Testimonial__c to Account and a lookup relationship from Testimonial__c to Contact.
Make both the Contact and Account fields required on the Testimonial__c object and create lookup relationships from Testimonial__c to Contact and to Account.
Create a lookup relationship from Testimonial__c to Account and a master-detail relationship from Testimonial__c to Contact.
Make Testimonial__c a junction object between Account and Contact using master-detail relationships.

sourceExplanation: Create a master-detail relationship from Testimonial__c to Account and a lookup relationship from Testimonial__c to Contact is the correct solution because master-detail relationships enforce cascade delete behavior. When the Account (master) is deleted, all related Testimonial__c records are automatically deleted. The lookup relationship to Contact allows the Contact to be deleted without affecting the Testimonial__c records. Why the other options are incorrect: Make both the Contact and Account fields required on the Testimonial__c object and create lookup relationships from Testimonial__c to Contact and to Account: Lookup relationships do not support cascade delete, so Testimonial__c records would remain even if the Account is deleted. Create a lookup relationship from Testimonial__c to Account and a master-detail relationship from Testimonial__c to Contact: This would cause Testimonial__c records to be deleted when the Contact is deleted, which contradicts the requirement. Make Testimonial__c a junction object between Account and Contact using master-detail relationships: A junction object with two master-detail relationships would cause Testimonial__c records to be deleted if either the Account or the Contact is deleted, which does not meet the business requirement.

stem: Universal Containers wants to ensure that they are accepting clean data from their users and verify that important fields are entered. What should an app builder recommend to meet this requirement?

options.text: Configure a validation to require a field for a specific record type.
Create a Flow to clean any data that is formatted wrong.
Make a formula field to check the format of the important fields.
Update the important fields to be required on the page layout.

sourceExplanation: Configure a validation to require a field for a specific record type is the correct recommendation because validation rules enforce data quality by preventing records from being saved unless required conditions are met. They can be tailored to specific record types and ensure important fields are completed correctly. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a Flow to clean any data that is formatted wrong: Flows run after user input and do not prevent users from saving incorrect or incomplete data. Make a formula field to check the format of the important fields: Formula fields can evaluate or display data but cannot stop users from saving records with missing or invalid values. Update the important fields to be required on the page layout: Page layout–required fields apply only to specific layouts and can be bypassed through imports, APIs, or automation, making them less reliable for enforcing clean data.

stem: A new field is being created on a custom object. However, the app builder does not want the field to show up on pre-existing custom report types. What should the app builder do on the custom field setup to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Deselect auto add to custom report type.
Remove the new field from all page layouts.
Remove visibility to all report profiles.
Grant read-only access to all report profiles.

sourceExplanation: Deselect auto add to custom report type is the correct action because this option controls whether a newly created field is automatically included in existing custom report types. By deselecting it, the field will not appear in pre-existing custom report types. Why the other options are incorrect: Remove the new field from all page layouts: Page layouts do not control whether fields are available in custom report types. Remove visibility to all report profiles: Field-level security affects user access to the field but does not prevent the field from being added to custom report types. Grant read-only access to all report profiles: Read-only access still allows the field to appear in reports and does not meet the requirement.
