stem: Universal Containers has deployed custom tabs to production via change sets, without including the profile settings or permission sets. What is the setting for the visibility of custom tabs?

options.text: Custom tabs are default on for all users.
Custom tabs are hidden for all users.
Custom tabs are default off for all users.

sourceExplanation: Custom tabs are default off for all users is the correct answer because when custom tabs are deployed via change sets without including profile or permission set settings, Salesforce sets the tab visibility to Default Off. Users must be granted access through profiles or permission sets after deployment. Why the other options are incorrect: Custom tabs are default on for all users: Tab visibility must be explicitly enabled through profiles or permission sets and is not automatically turned on. Custom tabs are hidden for all users: Hidden is different from Default Off and would require an explicit profile or permission set configuration. Custom tabs are NOT deployed: Custom tabs themselves are deployed successfully via change sets; only the visibility settings are not included.

stem: Universal Containers wants users to have access to the pricing guidelines document when viewing a Contract related to an Account. Which feature should an app builder use to create easy access to the document?

options.text: A custom detail page link on the Contract object
Quick Action on the Contracts object
A custom detail page link on the Account object
Quick Action on the Account object

sourceExplanation: A custom detail page link on the Contract object is the correct solution because it allows the app builder to add a direct link to the pricing guidelines document on the Contract record page. Users can easily access the document while viewing the Contract without navigating away from the record. Why the other options are incorrect: Quick Action on the Contracts object: Quick Actions are intended for creating or updating records, sending emails, or launching flows—not for providing direct links to external documents. A custom detail page link on the Account object: Placing the link on the Account page would require users to navigate away from the Contract to access the document, reducing efficiency. Quick Action on the Account object: Similar to the Contracts object, Quick Actions on Account are for actions like creating or updating records, not for providing direct document access.

stem: What are the limitations of Schema Builder when creating a custom object?

options.text: "Saw" should be clicked each time a new object, field, or relationship is created.
Relationships can be made to any custom objects, but any relationships to standard objects should be built in Lightning Object Manager.
Fields and relationships can be created, but they will be unable to add the fields to the page layout from the canvas.
Custom fields can be added to any custom objects, excluding formula field types.

sourceExplanation: Fields and relationships can be created, but they will be unable to add the fields to the page layout from the canvas is the correct limitation because Schema Builder allows you to create objects, fields, and relationships visually, but it does not support adding newly created fields directly to page layouts. Page layout adjustments must be done separately in Object Manager. Why the other options are incorrect: "Saw" should be clicked each time a new object, field, or relationship is created: There is no such requirement in Schema Builder; this is not a real limitation. Relationships can be made to any custom objects, but any relationships to standard objects should be built in Lightning Object Manager: Schema Builder can create relationships to both custom and standard objects, though some relationship types (like polymorphic lookups) may require Object Manager. This statement is misleading as a limitation. Custom fields can be added to any custom objects, excluding formula field types: Schema Builder supports creating formula fields, so this is not a true limitation.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) wants to quickly insert a list of over 1 million net new Accounts. The template based on CK's data model was used to populate the list. Which tool should be used?
sourceExplanation: Data Loader is the correct tool because it can handle large volumes of data—over 1 million records—and allows for bulk insertion of new Accounts using a CSV file. It supports inserting, updating, upserting, and deleting records efficiently. Why the other options are incorrect: Import Wizard: The Import Wizard is intended for smaller data loads (up to 50,000 records) and does not support very large datasets efficiently. Schema Builder: Schema Builder is used to create or modify objects and fields, not to import large volumes of data. Lightning Object Creator: Lightning Object Creator is designed to quickly create new objects and simple data collection apps, not for bulk importing millions of records.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to display 12 key fields at once in a separate section at the top of opportunity records on the desktop. Which component should an app builder add to the record page to enable this functionality?
sourceExplanation: Highlights Panel is the correct component because it displays key fields at the top of a record page on desktop, allowing users to see important information at a glance. It can be configured to show up to 12 fields in a dedicated section for easy visibility. Why the other options are incorrect: Path: Path is used to guide users through stages of a process, such as Opportunity stages, but does not display multiple fields in a dedicated section. Custom Lightning Web Component: While a custom component could be built to display fields, using the standard Highlights Panel is simpler and requires no custom development. Accordion: Accordion sections are used to organize content into collapsible sections, not to prominently display key fields at the top of a record page.

stem: The marketing director is concerned that too many car parts were given away for free last year. They want to track discounts, samples, and giveaways by Sales Rep. The manager's sign-off on free parts also needs to be processed. Which functionality should an app builder use to meet these requirements?
sourceExplanation: Approval process is the correct functionality because it allows the organization to enforce a manager’s sign-off before free car parts are given away. Approval processes can automate the routing of records for approval and track which Sales Rep requested discounts, samples, or giveaways. Why the other options are incorrect: Quotes: Quotes are used to generate price quotes for customers and do not handle approval workflows or track free items specifically. Check box: A checkbox can indicate a free item, but it cannot enforce manager approval or track approvals systematically. High Velocity Sales: High Velocity Sales is focused on automating sales cadences and lead management; it does not provide approval routing or tracking for free items.

stem: A Cloud Kicks employee submitted an opportunity for approval by their manager. What will happen if the employee attempts to edit the description field after submission?

options.text: User will see the record is now owned by their manager.
User will be presented with a 'Record Lock' notification.
User will be able to edit the name, but unable to edit the description.
User will be able to edit the description field only.

sourceExplanation: User will be presented with a 'Record Lock' notification is the correct outcome because when an opportunity is submitted for approval, Salesforce automatically locks the record to prevent edits. This ensures the approval process is based on the original data and maintains data integrity. Why the other options are incorrect: User will see the record is now owned by their manager: Submitting a record for approval does not change its ownership; ownership remains the same unless explicitly reassigned. User will be able to edit the name, but unable to edit the description: Record locking applies to the entire record, not specific fields, so no fields can be edited by the submitter. User will be able to edit the description field only: The submitter cannot edit any fields while the record is locked during the approval process.

stem: Universal Containers has a single Contact Lightning record page. A component takes up a lot of room on the page and is NOT needed by users with a Marketing profile. What should the app builder use to solve this issue?
sourceExplanation: Component visibility filter is the correct solution because it allows the app builder to show or hide a Lightning component based on user attributes, such as profile, role, or record data. In this case, the component can be hidden for users with the Marketing profile, improving page usability. Why the other options are incorrect: Detail page layouts: Page layouts control field placement and sections, but do not control individual Lightning component visibility on a Lightning record page. Field-level security: Field-level security controls access to field data, not entire components on a page. AppExchange: AppExchange is a marketplace for apps and components and does not provide functionality for controlling component visibility on a page.

stem: Due to the complexity of the Universal Containers sandbox release schedule and requirements, it is advised that change sets are used as often as possible to migrate from one environment to another. Which three common items can an app builder move when using a change set?
sourceExplanation: Apex class is a correct item because change sets can deploy custom Apex classes between Salesforce environments. Custom field is a correct item because change sets allow migration of custom fields, including their definitions and metadata. Custom object is a correct item because change sets can include entire custom objects, including associated fields, relationships, and page layouts. Why the other options are incorrect: Web-to-lead: Web-to-lead settings are not supported in change sets; they must be configured manually in each environment. Standard fields: Standard fields cannot be moved via change sets because they exist by default in Salesforce and cannot be customized for migration purposes.

stem: Cloud Kicks is redefining its entire business process to convert the Manager Notes field from a long text area field. The goal is to encourage managers to be more concise in their comments and stay at 255 characters or less. There is preexisting information in the Manager Notes field that often is well beyond the character limit. What would happen to any existing information if the app builder tries to convert a preexisting long text area field to text area?

options.text: Preexisting information in the field will be completely lost.
Preexisting information will cause an error message to pop up.
Preexisting information will remain even if it was over 255 characters.
Preexisting information will truncate to the first 255 characters.

sourceExplanation: Preexisting information will truncate to the first 255 characters is the correct outcome because when a Long Text Area field is converted to a Text Area (255 characters), Salesforce automatically truncates any existing content that exceeds the 255-character limit. Data beyond the limit will be permanently removed. Why the other options are incorrect: Preexisting information in the field will be completely lost: Only the portion of text beyond 255 characters is lost; the first 255 characters are preserved. Preexisting information will cause an error message to pop up: Salesforce allows the conversion but truncates the excess text; it does not block the conversion with an error. Preexisting information will remain even if it was over 255 characters: Salesforce cannot retain content beyond the Text Area limit, so content over 255 characters will be truncated.

stem: An app builder needs a custom solution and is considering using either AppExchange or their local developer community. The app builder wants to minimize the need for manual maintenance. What should the app builder consider?
sourceExplanation: A managed package from AppExchange is the correct choice because managed packages are maintained by the provider, can be upgraded easily, and reduce the need for ongoing manual maintenance. They offer packaged functionality that is supported and can include automated updates. Why the other options are incorrect: An open-source custom development: While flexible, open-source custom development requires the app builder to maintain and update the code manually, increasing maintenance effort. An unmanaged package from AppExchange: Unmanaged packages provide code and components but do not support upgrades or automated maintenance, so the app builder must handle updates manually. An open-source unmanaged package: This approach also requires manual maintenance and does not provide the upgrade or support benefits of a managed package.

stem: A custom field on an account is used to track finance information about a customer. Only members of the finance team have access to this field. However, the business wants to allow one customer service agent, who is assigned the Customer Service profile, read-only access to this field for special circumstances. What is the recommended solution to grant the customer service agent access to the field?

options.text: Update the custom field's field level security in setup to allow the agent read-only access to the field.
Create a new profile to allow for read-only access to the field via field level security and assign it to the agent.
Create a permission set that allows read-only access to the field via field level security and assign it to the agent.
Update the Customer Service Profile already assigned to the agent to allow for read-only access to the field via field level security.

sourceExplanation: Create a permission set that allows read-only access to the field via field-level security and assign it to the agent is the correct solution because permission sets provide a flexible way to grant additional access to specific users without changing their profile. This allows the single Customer Service agent to view the finance field while keeping it restricted for all other non-finance users. Why the other options are incorrect: Update the custom field's field-level security in setup to allow the agent read-only access to the field: Field-level security changes apply to profiles, not individual users, so this cannot target a single agent. Create a new profile to allow for read-only access to the field via field-level security and assign it to the agent: Creating a new profile for a single user is unnecessary and adds administrative complexity; permission sets are preferred for exceptions. Update the Customer Service Profile already assigned to the agent to allow for read-only access to the field via field-level security: Changing the profile would grant access to all users with the Customer Service profile, not just the one agent, which violates the requirement.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to make sure that users without the Marketing role are unable to update the Contact Retail Opt In picklist field to Yes. Which validation rule should an app builder use to prevent other users from making this update?
sourceExplanation: The correct validation rule should check that the user's role is NOT Marketing, that the Retail_Opt_In__c field is being changed, and that the new value is "Yes". This prevents non-Marketing users from updating the field to "Yes". The correct syntax is: AND( $UserRole.Name != 'Marketing', ISCHANGED(Retail_Opt_In__c), ISPICKVAL(Retail_Opt_In__c, "Yes") ) Why the other options are incorrect: Options A and B do not check if the field is being changed (ISCHANGED). Option C incorrectly checks for Marketing users instead of non-Marketing users.

stem: Universal Containers expects impacts to operations due to increased demand. The executive team will reach out to current customers and wants to see the number of open cases for the account and parent account. What should an app builder use to display the number of open cases on the account page?
sourceExplanation: Roll-up summary is the correct solution because it allows the app builder to calculate and display aggregated data, such as the number of open cases, directly on a parent record like an Account. Roll-up summary fields automatically update when related child records (Cases) are created, updated, or deleted. Why the other options are incorrect: Flow: While a Flow could calculate and update a field, it requires more setup and manual maintenance compared to a native roll-up summary field. Custom object: A custom object is not needed for this purpose because the relationship and aggregation already exist between Accounts and Cases. Approval Process: Approval processes are used to route records for approvals and cannot calculate or display aggregated data.

stem: Ursa Major Solar wants to automate a welcome email to new clients and include a customized survey about their buying experience. An app builder is tasked with this project and has very little time to build the solution from scratch, but still needs to be able to fully customize the solution. What should the app builder do to meet the deadline and custom requirements?

options.text: Choose an unmanaged package from AppExchange that closely meets the requirements of the project and allows programmatic development.
Choose a managed package from AppExchange that closely meets the requirements of the project, restricts programmatic development, but allows declarative development.
Work with a developer to create custom Apex code and a lightning web component survey to meet the criteria.
Use Salesforce flow to build the survey declaratively to meet the criteria and send it to the customer as an email.

sourceExplanation: Use Salesforce Flow to build the survey declaratively to meet the criteria and send it to the customer as an email is the correct solution because Flows allow rapid, fully declarative automation. The app builder can create a survey, collect responses, and automatically send a welcome email without writing code, meeting both the tight deadline and customization requirements. Why the other options are incorrect: Choose an unmanaged package from AppExchange that closely meets the requirements of the project and allows programmatic development: Unmanaged packages require additional setup and ongoing maintenance, and they may not fully meet the customization or time requirements. Choose a managed package from AppExchange that closely meets the requirements of the project, restricts programmatic development, but allows declarative development: Managed packages may restrict customization and programmatic flexibility, which could prevent fully tailoring the survey or email experience. Work with a developer to create custom Apex code and a Lightning Web Component survey to meet the criteria: Custom development requires significantly more time and resources, which conflicts with the need for a quick solution.

stem: Cloud Kicks has a sales rep who is stating that their Contact is unavailable for other users to see within Salesforce. In which three ways can an app builder troubleshoot this issue?

options.text: Verify the users with the issue have access to the Contact object.
Review the Contact record and ensure it is linked to an Account.
Create a new Contact and have the users try again.
Create an Account Sharing Rule to give the users access to all records.
Confirm whether Default Organization-Wide Sharing Settings provide access to the Account.

sourceExplanation: Verify the users with the issue have access to the Contact object is correct because object-level permissions control whether a user can view any records of that object. If the users lack “Read” access to Contacts, they will not see any Contact records. Review the Contact record and ensure it is linked to an Account is correct because Contacts must be associated with an Account to inherit sharing from the parent. A Contact without an Account may have more restricted visibility depending on org settings. Confirm whether Default Organization-Wide Sharing Settings provide access to the Account is correct because sharing settings on the parent Account control access to related Contacts. If the Account is private, users may be unable to see the Contact even if they have object-level access. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a new Contact and have the users try again: Creating a new Contact does not address why the existing Contact is not visible. Create an Account Sharing Rule to give the users access to all records: This is only necessary if sharing rules are required; it is not a troubleshooting step but a configuration change.

stem: Universal Containers has the Account object's Organization-Wide Default set to Private. The marketing team owns Accounts; however, they also need to be able to see the sales team's Accounts. Both the sales and marketing teams are in completely different branches of the role hierarchy. Which feature should be used to enable marketing to see sales-owned accounts?
sourceExplanation: Sharing rules is the correct feature because they allow records to be shared automatically with users outside the role hierarchy. Since marketing and sales teams are in different branches of the role hierarchy, sharing rules can grant marketing users read or read/write access to Accounts owned by the sales team while maintaining the Account object's Private OWD. Why the other options are incorrect: Assignment rules: Assignment rules automatically assign records to users or queues but do not grant visibility to users who do not own the records. Public groups: Public groups are used to define groups of users for sharing purposes, but by themselves, they do not grant access; they are used in conjunction with sharing rules. Aliases: Aliases are short names used to identify users in emails or reports and have no effect on record access.

stem: DreamHouse Realty wants to import its property records from an external system into Salesforce. The app builder will use an external ID field to house the property ID from the external system. Which two details should the app builder know when using external ID fields?

options.text: An external ID field can be an auto-number field.
Each org can have up to 25 custom external ID fields.
An external ID field can be a URL field.
Each object can have up to 25 custom external ID fields.

sourceExplanation: An external ID field can be an auto-number field is correct because external ID fields can be of type Text, Number, or Auto-Number, allowing Salesforce to use them as unique identifiers for record matching during imports or upserts. Each object can have up to 25 custom external ID fields is correct because Salesforce limits the number of custom external ID fields per object to 25. These fields can be used for integration or data import purposes. Why the other options are incorrect: Each org can have up to 25 custom external ID fields: The limit applies per object, not per org. An external ID field can be a URL field: URL fields cannot be designated as external ID fields; only Text, Number, or Auto-Number fields are supported.

stem: The VP of Sales at Universal Containers has asked the app builder to let sales reps create opportunity records directly from the account, with a number of fields pre-populated. Which feature should the app builder use to allow users to create the opportunity?
sourceExplanation: Quick action is the correct feature because it allows users to create related records, like Opportunities from an Account, and supports pre-populating fields. Quick actions can be added to the page layout or Salesforce mobile app, enabling streamlined record creation with default values. Why the other options are incorrect: Custom link: Custom links can navigate to URLs or external systems but do not provide the same seamless record creation with pre-populated fields. Default action: Default actions define which standard action appears when a user clicks the record tab but do not allow customization of pre-populated fields for new records. Custom button: Custom buttons can perform similar actions but are less flexible than Quick Actions for pre-populating fields and integrating with the Lightning Experience interface.

stem: Universal Containers allows all employees to submit reviews for leadership using a custom object called Review. These Reviews should only be visible to the HR department and the employee who submitted the record. Which three steps should an app builder take to properly control access to Reviews?

options.text: Remove Review Read permission from non-HR Department user Profiles.
Add a Master-Detail(User) field on the Review object.
Create a criteria-based Sharing Rule for the HR Department.

sourceExplanation: Remove Review Read permission from non-HR Department user Profiles ensures only HR users have object-level access to Review records. Set organization-wide default to Private ensures that only record owners and users explicitly granted access can see the records. Create a criteria-based Sharing Rule for the HR Department automatically shares Review records with HR users, allowing them to see all Reviews regardless of ownership. Why the other options are incorrect: Disable Grant Access Using Hierarchies: This would prevent managers from accessing records of their subordinates, which is not required in this scenario. Add a Master-Detail(User) field on the Review object: This would create a relationship with the User object but is unnecessary for meeting the sharing requirements.

stem: Sales reps at Cloud Kicks (CK) forget to submit for approval when CK needs orders reviewed before close won. CK wants to automatically submit opportunities into the Secure Commitment Stage to eliminate manual submission. Which feature meets the business requirements?

options.text: Record Triggered flow optimized for Fast Field Updates
Record-Triggered flow optimized for Actions and Related Records

sourceExplanation: Record-Triggered Flow optimized for Actions and Related Records is the correct feature because it can automatically submit Opportunities for approval when they meet certain criteria, such as entering the Secure Commitment Stage. This type of flow can perform actions on the record and related records without requiring user intervention, eliminating the need for manual submission. Why the other options are incorrect: Record-Triggered Flow optimized for Fast Field Updates: This flow type is limited to updating the triggering record only and cannot perform actions like submitting for approval or updating related records. Custom button and screen flow: This approach requires manual user interaction, which does not meet the requirement for automatic submission. Platform Event-Triggered Flow: Platform event–triggered flows respond to external events, not changes on standard records like Opportunity stage updates.

stem: Ursa Major Solar (UMS) has a custom object where they track Galactic Vendors. The object has four custom fields for the Galactic Vendors's location: Street (Street__c), City (City__c), Planet (Planet__c), Galaxy (Galaxy__c). The UMS's leadership wants these fields to be combined into a single formula field on two lines. Which formula fulfills this requirement?
sourceExplanation: Street__c & BR() & City__c & "," & Planet__c & "" & Galaxy__c is the correct formula because it concatenates the four location fields into a single formula field and uses BR() to insert a line break between the street and the rest of the address. This displays the address on two lines as requested. Why the other options are incorrect: Street__c City__c, Planet__c Galaxy__c: This syntax is invalid in Salesforce formulas because it does not use & to concatenate fields or values. Street__c, City__c & Planet__c & Galaxy__c: This formula does not include a line break and incorrectly places commas, so it will not format the address on two lines.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to display the number of Opportunity records associated with each Account. Which solution should be used?
sourceExplanation: Roll-up summary field is the correct solution because it allows Salesforce to automatically calculate and display aggregate data, such as the number of Opportunities related to an Account. Roll-up summary fields work on master-detail relationships and update dynamically when child records are added, edited, or deleted. Why the other options are incorrect: Formula field: Formula fields can reference related fields but cannot count child records. AppExchange offering: While third-party solutions might provide similar functionality, Salesforce’s native roll-up summary field is simpler and does not require additional installations. Lookup field: Lookup fields establish a relationship between records but do not perform aggregation or counting of related records.

stem: A user is unable to use inline editing on a list view. A quick check verifies the user should be able to perform inline editing as they have been assigned the appropriate permissions. Which condition should the app builder review?

options.text: If the list view restricts sharing for the user
If the list view contains a chart created by the user
If the list view selected is locked by another user
If the list view contains more than one record type

sourceExplanation: If the list view contains more than one record type is the correct condition to review because Salesforce does not allow inline editing on list views that include multiple record types. Inline editing is only supported when all records in the view share the same record type, even if the user has the appropriate permissions. Why the other options are incorrect: If the list view restricts sharing for the user: Sharing settings affect visibility of records but do not prevent inline editing if the user has edit access. If the list view contains a chart created by the user: Charts on a list view do not affect the ability to perform inline editing. If the list view selected is locked by another user: List views themselves are not “locked” by users; locking applies to records, not views, so this does not prevent inline editing on editable records.

stem: Managers at Universal Containers want a quick way to create additional accounts to form a hierarchy from a Parent Account record. They want to auto-populate five fields based on the parent to make it easier for users to create the child accounts quickly. What should the app builder recommend?

options.text: Add a custom link on Account

sourceExplanation: Customize a Global Quick Action is the correct recommendation because Global Quick Actions can be configured to create records (like child Accounts) from a parent record page, with fields pre-populated from the parent. This provides a streamlined way for managers to create child Accounts with inherited values directly from the parent Account page.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) wants to track orders against inventory, ensuring its ability to fulfill order requests. CK created a junction object called Request Inventory to enable many-to-many relationships with the Inventory and Order objects. What does the app builder need to provide to ensure users can view Request Inventory records?

options.text: Sharing rules on Request Inventory object.
Read access to the first master object.
Apex-based sharing on the first master object.
Read access to both master objects.

sourceExplanation: Read access to both master objects is the correct requirement because a junction object uses two master-detail relationships, and access to the junction object records is controlled by the access to both parent (master) objects. Users must have at least read access to both master objects (Inventory and Order) to view related Request Inventory records. Why the other options are incorrect: Sharing rules on Request Inventory object: Sharing rules cannot override the inherent master-detail sharing model of a junction object. Read access to the first master object: Access to only one master object is insufficient; access to both masters is required. Apex-based sharing on the first master object: Apex sharing cannot grant access to junction object records if the user lacks access to both master objects.

stem: When an opportunity has a closed date that is pushed more than 30 days, manager approval is required. An approval process is in place but reps frequently forget to submit for approval to run the process. How can an app builder ensure that these opportunities are submitted into the approval process?

options.text: Give the manager the "API Enabled" permission to permit approval responses by email.
Use a validation rule and an email alert to the manager requesting approval.
Submit the record for approval from an automated process.
Change the entry criteria on the approval process to criteria are met and lock the record on initial submission.

sourceExplanation: Submit the record for approval from an automated process is the correct solution because an app builder can use a record-triggered Flow or Process Builder to automatically submit Opportunities for approval when the closed date is pushed more than 30 days. This eliminates the need for manual submission by sales reps. Why the other options are incorrect: Give the manager the "API Enabled" permission to permit approval responses by email: This addresses how approvals can be responded to but does not automate submission. Use a validation rule and an email alert to the manager requesting approval: This only notifies the manager but does not submit the record for approval automatically. Change the entry criteria on the approval process to criteria are met and lock the record on initial submission: This controls which records can enter the process and locking behavior but does not automate submission.

stem: Service Agents are required to confirm a user's identity before providing support information over the phone. Which feature can an app builder use to help agents meet this requirement?

options.text: Include Surveys as a Case related list
Guided Action Flows on the record page
Add Path to the top of the Case layout

sourceExplanation: Add Path to the top of the Case layout is the correct solution because Path can guide service agents through a step-by-step process, including identity verification steps, directly on the Case record page. This ensures agents follow the required verification process before proceeding with support.

stem: After utilizing the Lightning Object Creator to create a new object, its fields, and to insert all of the data, an app builder now needs to set up the Lightning Record Page. Which component should the app builder have on their Lightning Record Page to see all of the fields from the page layout?
sourceExplanation: Record Detail is the correct component because it displays all fields from the page layout on the Lightning Record Page. This component automatically reflects the fields, sections, and field order configured in the page layout, allowing users to view and edit data as intended. Why the other options are incorrect: Path: Path is used to guide users through stages in a process, like Opportunity stages, and does not display all fields from a page layout. Recommendations: Recommendations provide actionable suggestions, such as next steps or system prompts, and do not display record fields. Highlights Panel: Highlights Panel shows key fields at the top of the record page but only displays a limited number of fields and does not reflect the full page layout.

stem: Universal Containers needs the 18-digit record ID from Opportunity records when exporting data to Excel in order to ensure each record is treated uniquely. Which formula should an app builder use to create this new field?
sourceExplanation: TEXT(14) is the correct approach because it converts the 15-character Salesforce record ID to a text string, allowing the app builder to export the full 18-character ID. In Salesforce, the 15-character ID is case-sensitive, and converting it to text or using the standard 18-character ID ensures uniqueness when exporting to Excel. Why the other options are incorrect: VALUE(14): VALUE() converts text to a number, which is not applicable for Salesforce record IDs. ISNUMBER(14): ISNUMBER() checks if a value is numeric; record IDs are alphanumeric, so this does not work. CAREBAFFIELD(14): This is not a valid Salesforce formula function.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) has large data volumes and is nearing data storage limits. The planned solution is to archive historical data to reduce data storage in Salesforce; however, UC would still like to use reports, queries, and lookups on the archived information. Which two options could meet this requirement?
sourceExplanation: Big Objects is correct because Salesforce Big Objects are designed to store and manage massive volumes of data while still allowing reporting, queries (via Async SOQL), and lookups. They are ideal for archiving historical data without impacting standard data storage limits. External Objects is correct because external objects allow Salesforce to access data stored outside of Salesforce, such as in external databases or cloud storage, while still enabling reporting and lookups through Salesforce Connect. This approach avoids using Salesforce data storage. Why the other options are incorrect: Related Objects: “Related objects” is not a standard Salesforce feature or storage solution; it does not provide a mechanism for managing large volumes of archived data. Custom Objects: Custom objects store data in Salesforce standard storage, so using them for large historical datasets would not reduce storage usage.

stem: Ursa Major Solar's service department gets requests for several types of services, such as installation, repair, and maintenance. Service managers need to be able to tell when maintenance was last done on an asset to help determine if they are meeting contract agreements, but the last maintenance date can be difficult to determine when there are many work orders related to the asset. They think it would be helpful to have a field auto-populated on the Asset record when a maintenance work order gets closed. Which tool should an app builder recommend to help meet this requirement?
sourceExplanation: Roll-up Summary is the correct tool because it can automatically calculate and display the maximum (latest) date from related child records (Work Orders) on the parent Asset record. By configuring a roll-up summary field to find the MAX Close Date of related maintenance Work Orders, service managers can easily see when the last maintenance was performed.

stem: An app builder installed a custom Lightning component from AppExchange. What should be done next in order to configure the component for use in a record page?

options.text: Edit a record page using the Page Layout editor > Drag the component onto the page.
Edit a record page using App Manager > Drag the component onto the page.
Edit a record page using Lightning App Builder > Drag the component onto the page.
Edit a record page using the Page Layout editor > Drag the Visualforce component onto the page.

sourceExplanation: Edit a record page using Lightning App Builder > Drag the component onto the page is the correct next step because custom Lightning components from AppExchange are added to record pages through the Lightning App Builder. This allows the app builder to place the component in the desired section of the page and configure its properties. Why the other options are incorrect: Edit a record page using the Page Layout editor > Drag the component onto the page: The Page Layout editor only controls fields, sections, and standard related lists; it cannot add Lightning components. Edit a record page using App Manager > Drag the component onto the page: App Manager is used to manage apps, not to edit record pages or place components. Edit a record page using the Page Layout editor > Drag the Visualforce component onto the page: This applies only to Visualforce pages, not Lightning components installed from AppExchange.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to know the total value of all won Opportunities for Accounts and display it on the record. Which type of summary should the app builder use in the roll-up summary field?
sourceExplanation: Sum is the correct type of summary to use in a roll-up summary field because it calculates the total value of a specific numeric field (e.g., Opportunity Amount) for all related child records that meet the filter criteria (e.g., Stage = Closed Won). Why the other options are incorrect: Aggregate: “Aggregate” is not a roll-up summary type in Salesforce; Salesforce provides Sum, Min, Max, and Count. Total: There is no roll-up summary type called Total; Sum serves this purpose. Count: Count only counts the number of related records and does not calculate the total value of a numeric field.

stem: An app builder at Northern Trail Outfitters created a sandbox template for Accounts, Projects, and Project Milestones to reconfigure some flows for the project management app. Which type of testing environment should the app builder create?
sourceExplanation: Partial Copy is the correct solution because partial copy sandboxes include a subset of production data along with all metadata, allowing the app builder to test flows and configurations in a realistic environment without needing the full dataset. This makes it ideal for testing processes like Accounts, Projects, and Project Milestones while minimizing storage and setup time. Why the other options are incorrect: Developer Pro: Developer Pro sandboxes have more storage than Developer sandboxes but do not include production data by default. They are better for building and testing metadata-heavy changes, not for testing with actual record data. Developer: Developer sandboxes are intended for individual development and contain only metadata, with no production data included. They are not suitable when testing flows that rely on existing Accounts, Projects, or Project Milestones. Scratch Org: Scratch orgs are temporary environments primarily used for development and testing with source-driven workflows. They do not include production data unless explicitly imported, making them less ideal for testing existing record-based flows.

stem: The Director of Customer Service wants to receive a notification when a case stays in the new status for more than four business hours. Which two automation processes should be used to accomplish this?
sourceExplanation: Escalation Rules and Scheduled Apex are the correct solutions because: Escalation Rules can automatically notify users or managers when a case meets certain criteria, such as remaining in a specific status for a defined amount of time. They are designed specifically to handle time-based case notifications. Scheduled Apex allows developers to run custom code at scheduled intervals, so it can check cases that have been in the new status for more than four business hours and trigger notifications if needed. Why the other options are incorrect: Validation Rule: Validation rules are used to enforce data integrity when a user creates or edits a record. They cannot send notifications based on elapsed time. Flow Builder: While Flow Builder can automate many processes, standard record-triggered flows do not natively handle precise business-hour time-based actions without additional configuration or scheduled flows. On its own, it’s not the most straightforward solution for this time-based notification requirement.

stem: DreamHouse Realty is rethinking its sandbox utilization strategy after acquiring Cloud Kicks. The Salesforce COE already utilizes a partial and a full sandbox, which it refreshes on their own regular schedules. Teams are expanding and have to begin each of their small projects in a sandbox before committing to the larger pool for collaborative testing while still keeping costs down. Which sandbox type should be considered first?
sourceExplanation: Developer sandbox is the correct solution because it provides each team member with an isolated environment to start small projects without impacting others. Developer sandboxes are low-cost, include only metadata (no production data), and can be refreshed frequently, making them ideal for individual development and initial testing before moving to larger shared sandboxes. Why the other options are incorrect: Developer Pro sandbox: Developer Pro sandboxes offer more storage than Developer sandboxes, but for small individual projects, the extra storage is usually unnecessary, making them less cost-efficient. Full sandbox: Full sandboxes replicate all production data and metadata, making them expensive and unnecessary for small, isolated projects that don't require full production data. Partial sandbox: Partial sandboxes include a subset of production data and are better suited for more advanced testing or collaborative projects rather than initial individual development.

stem: The app builder at Ursa Major Solar created a master-detail relationship between a parent object Galaxy_c and child object Star_c. What is the effect of creating this type of relationship if users want to report on Galaxy_c with Star_c?

options.text: A Galaxy_c with Star_c report type will be automatically created.
A Star_c report type with Galaxy_c as a field will be automatically created.
A new custom report type will need to be created for Star_c with lookup fields from Galaxy_c.
A new custom report type will need to be created for Galaxy_c with Star_c.

sourceExplanation: A Galaxy_c with Star_c report type will be automatically created because Salesforce automatically generates a "with" report type for master-detail relationships, allowing reporting on the parent object with related child records.

stem: Universal Containers is setting up Salesforce for the first time. Management wants the sales and marketing teams to have different navigation menus in the Salesforce Mobile App. Which option is available to an app builder to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Create roles for sales and marketing and assign a custom homepage layout for each role.
Create mobile navigation menus for both the sales and marketing profiles.
Create sales and marketing apps and assign the respective profiles to each app.
Create public groups for sales and marketing and create mobile navigation menus for each group.

sourceExplanation: Create sales and marketing apps and assign the respective profiles to each app is the correct solution because in Salesforce, each app can have a customized navigation menu in the Mobile App. By creating separate apps for sales and marketing and assigning the appropriate profiles, users see only the navigation items relevant to their team, ensuring a tailored experience. Why the other options are incorrect: Create roles for sales and marketing and assign a custom homepage layout for each role: Roles control record-level access, not the mobile navigation menu, so this does not achieve the desired menu customization. Create mobile navigation menus for both the sales and marketing profiles: Profiles can control app access and permissions but do not allow creation of separate mobile navigation menus directly; apps are required for menu customization. Create public groups for sales and marketing and create mobile navigation menus for each group: Public groups are used for sharing rules and access, not for customizing mobile navigation menus.

stem: At Ursa Major Solar, there is a single Lightning record page for the Celestial Bodies custom object; however, there is a Lightning component the app builder wants to restrict to mobile app users. Which feature in the Lightning app builder should be utilized?
sourceExplanation: Form factor checkboxes is the correct solution because they allow the app builder to control which devices a Lightning component appears on. By selecting only the mobile form factor, the component can be restricted to users accessing the Salesforce Mobile App, ensuring it doesn’t appear on desktop layouts. Why the other options are incorrect: Highlights panel: The highlights panel controls which key fields are displayed at the top of a record page but does not control component visibility based on device type. Related list quick links: Related list quick links manage how related records are displayed on a page but cannot restrict components to mobile users. Component visibility filter: Component visibility filters control whether a component appears based on record data, user fields, or permissions, not the device form factor.

stem: Which two report formats can be used as a source report to configure a reporting snapshot?
sourceExplanation: Tabular format and Summary format are the correct solutions because reporting snapshots can use these report types as source reports. Tabular reports provide simple row-by-row data, while summary reports allow grouping and aggregation, both of which can be captured in a snapshot for tracking historical data. Why the other options are incorrect: Matrix format: Matrix reports group data both by rows and columns and are not supported as source reports for reporting snapshots. Joined format: Joined reports combine multiple blocks of data into a single report, but Salesforce does not allow them to be used as source reports for reporting snapshots.

stem: Cloud Kicks conducts an evaluation of sales reps with a custom object that houses a scorecar The company wants to ensure that only the sales reps, their managers, and their manager's executives can view the reps scorecard, but also prevent the reps from being able to view the executive comment fields on their review. How should these requirements be met?

options.text: Use a private sharing model granting record access using hierarchy; manage field access with field-level security.
Use a private sharing model granting record access using custom settings; manage field access with page layouts and field-level security.
Use a private sharing model granting record access using custom settings; manage field access with record types and page layouts.
Use a private sharing model granting record access using hierarchy; manage field access with record types and field-level security.

sourceExplanation: Use a private sharing model granting record access using hierarchy; manage field access with record types and field-level security is the correct solution because a private sharing model ensures that only the record owner and users above them in the role hierarchy (managers and executives) can access the scorecard. Field-level security combined with record types allows sensitive fields, like executive comments, to be hidden from sales reps while still visible to managers and executives. Why the other options are incorrect: Use a private sharing model granting record access using hierarchy; manage field access with field-level security: Field-level security alone cannot restrict access based on the type of user or the context of the record (e.g., hiding executive comments only for reps). Use a private sharing model granting record access using custom settings; manage field access with page layouts and field-level security: Custom settings do not control record-level access and cannot enforce hierarchy-based access. Page layouts alone cannot prevent users from accessing fields through reports or API. Use a private sharing model granting record access using custom settings; manage field access with record types and page layouts: Custom settings are not used for record sharing. While record types and page layouts control field visibility in the UI, they do not enforce proper record-level security for managers and executives.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) switched to Lightning Experience and started using Chatter across its global workforce to support its fast-paced sales cycle. CK loves Chatter but struggle with gathering feedback from core team members, including understanding who is available to respond. Which two ways could CK use Chatter to solve this problem?
sourceExplanation: Polls and Out of Office are the correct solutions because they directly address gathering feedback and understanding team availability in Chatter: Polls allow team members to quickly provide feedback or vote on options, making it easy to gather input from the group efficiently. Out of Office lets users indicate when they are unavailable, helping others know who can respond and plan accordingly. Why the other options are incorrect: Topics: Topics help categorize and organize Chatter posts for easier searching but do not provide a way to actively gather feedback or indicate availability. Streams: Streams allow users to follow feeds, records, or groups in Chatter, improving visibility but not directly helping with collecting feedback or identifying available responders.

stem: DreamHouse Realty (DR) employees started using company-owned airplanes for work travel after Ursa Major Solar was acquired. DR executives want to automate the submission travel request forms to enforce the internal policy. How should an app builder automate travel requests based on these criteria?
sourceExplanation: Approval process is the correct solution because it automates the submission and review of travel request forms. Approval processes in Salesforce allow records to be routed automatically to the appropriate manager or executive for review and approval based on predefined criteria, ensuring that internal policies are enforced consistently. Why the other options are incorrect: Validation rule: Validation rules enforce data integrity by preventing users from saving records that don't meet certain conditions, but they do not automate the approval or submission workflow. Assignment rule: Assignment rules automatically assign ownership of records (like leads or cases) but do not provide a mechanism for review and approval workflows. Apex: Apex can automate almost any process, but using it for standard approval workflows is unnecessary when Salesforce provides declarative approval processes that are easier to maintain and configure.

stem: Universal Containers wants to collaborate with its customers within Salesforce and has decided to enable the Allow Customer Invitations in the Chatter settings. Which permission is granted to customers when invited to a Charter group?

options.text: The ability to invite members to groups of which they are a member.
The ability to interact with members of their groups.
The ability to @mention accounts of which they are a contact.
The ability to request access to public groups.

sourceExplanation: The ability to interact with members of their groups is the correct solution because when customers are invited to a Chatter group using the “Allow Customer Invitations” setting, they can post, comment, and like posts within that group. This enables collaboration between the company and its customers in a controlled environment. Why the other options are incorrect: The ability to invite members to groups of which they are a member: Customers cannot invite other members; only internal users with proper permissions can manage group membership. The ability to @mention accounts of which they are a contact: Customers can @mention people in the group but not accounts directly. The ability to request access to public groups: This permission is unrelated to Chatter group collaboration; it applies to requesting access to public groups, not interacting within an existing group.

stem: Universal Containers created a custom object called Component to capture details about products sold. Which approach should an app builder take to show Component as a related list on Product?

options.text: Create a master-detail relationship on Product to Component. Add the Component related list to the Product page layout.
Create a lookup relationship on Component to Product. Add the Component related list to the Product page layout.
Create a roll-up on Product. Add the Component related list to the Product page layout.
Create a junction object to relate Component and Product. Add the Component related list to the Product page layout.

sourceExplanation: Create a lookup relationship on Component to Product. Add the Component related list to the Product page layout is the correct solution because a lookup relationship allows Component records to be associated with a Product. Once the relationship is created, the related list for Component can be added to the Product page layout, enabling users to see all Components linked to that Product. Why the other options are incorrect: Create a master-detail relationship on Product to Component. Add the Component related list to the Product page layout: Master-detail relationships must be created on the child object, not the parent. You cannot create a master-detail from Product to Component directly. Create a roll-up on Product. Add the Component related list to the Product page layout: Roll-up summary fields aggregate data but do not establish a relationship that allows displaying a related list. Create a junction object to relate Component and Product. Add the Component related list to the Product page layout: A junction object is only needed for many-to-many relationships, which is unnecessary if a simple one-to-many relationship between Product and Component is sufficient.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) wants to test code against a subset of production data that is under 5 GB. Additionally, UC wants to refresh this sandbox every weekend. Which type of sandbox should be used to accomplish this?
sourceExplanation: Partial Copy is the correct solution because it allows a subset of production data (up to 5 GB) to be copied along with all metadata. Partial Copy sandboxes can be refreshed on a schedule, such as every weekend, making them ideal for testing with realistic data without the storage and refresh constraints of a full sandbox. Why the other options are incorrect: Full Copy: Full Copy sandboxes replicate all production data and metadata, are limited in number, take longer to refresh, and are unnecessary when only a subset of data is required. Developer: Developer sandboxes include only metadata and no production data, so they cannot be used to test against a subset of actual production records. Developer Pro: Developer Pro sandboxes provide more storage than Developer sandboxes but still contain only metadata, not production data, making them unsuitable for testing with real data.

stem: AW Computing has a custom object for service plans. A service plan needs to be associated to one and only one contact. The support manager noticed if the wrong contact is associated, the reps are unable to change the contact. The app builder already confirmed the user has correct access to the field and there are no validations associated with the service plans. What could be causing the issue?

options.text: The Allow reparenting checkbox, Child records can be reparented to other parent records after they are created, is unchecked.
The Read/Write radio button, Allows users with at least Read/Write access to the Master record to create, edit, or delete related Detail records, is selected.
The Allow reparenting checkbox, Child records can be reparented to other parent records after they are created, is checked.
The Read Only radio button, Allows users with at least Read access to the Master record to create, edit, or delete related Detail records, is selected.

sourceExplanation: The Allow reparenting checkbox, Child records can be reparented to other parent records after they are created, is unchecked is the correct solution because when a master-detail relationship is created, the child record (Service Plan) is locked to its parent (Contact) unless the Allow reparenting option is enabled. Without this option checked, users cannot change the parent record after the child record is created, even if they have full field and record access. Why the other options are incorrect: The Read/Write radio button, Allows users with at least Read/Write access to the Master record to create, edit, or delete related Detail records, is selected: This controls the ability to create, edit, or delete child records, not to change the parent record. The Allow reparenting checkbox, Child records can be reparented to other parent records after they are created, is checked: If this were checked, users would be able to change the parent record, so this cannot be the cause of the issue. The Read Only radio button, Allows users with at least Read access to the Master record to create, edit, or delete related Detail records, is selected: This restricts edits to the child record but does not directly relate to the ability to reparent the record.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) tracks Account locations in Zip Code, a custom text field with a validation rule to enforce proper formatting of the US ZIP+4 code for UC's orders. Which formula should the app builder create on Order to display only the first five digits of Zip Code from the parent Account?
sourceExplanation: LEFT(Account.zip_Code__c, 5) is the correct solution because the LEFT function extracts a specified number of characters from the beginning of a text string. In this case, it retrieves the first five digits of the ZIP+4 code from the parent Account’s zip_Code__c field. Why the other options are incorrect: TEXT(Account.zip_Code__c, $): The TEXT function converts numbers or dates to text but does not extract a portion of a text string. BEGINS(Account.zip_Code__r, $): The BEGINS function checks whether a text string starts with a specific substring and returns a boolean (TRUE/FALSE), not a portion of the string. LPAD(Account.zip_Code__r, $): The LPAD function pads the left side of a string with additional characters; it does not extract the first characters from a text field.

stem: The app builder at AW Computing has been asked to track the number of times a case has been reopened. Which solution should the app builder utilize to help with this request?
sourceExplanation: Record-triggered flow is the correct solution because it can automatically run when a Case record is updated. By configuring the flow to trigger on edits, the app builder can check if the Case’s status changed from “Closed” or “Resolved” back to “Open” and increment a custom “Reopen Count” field, all without writing Apex code. Why the other options are incorrect: Apex Trigger: While an Apex trigger could accomplish this, it requires custom code. Salesforce recommends using declarative tools like flows when possible. Scheduled Triggered flow: Scheduled flows run at specified times, not immediately when a record is updated, so they cannot track real-time case reopen events efficiently. Screen Flow: Screen flows require user interaction to run, which is not suitable for automatically tracking status changes on Cases.

stem: A new field has been added to the Applicant object that is part of an unmanaged package. A recruiter ran the Position with or without Applicants report and noticed that the new field was missing as an option to add as a column. How should an app builder troubleshoot this issue?

options.text: Adjust the field level security to include in the report type.
Check Allow Reports for the position and applicant objects.
Update the profile with the Manage Public Reports permission.
Add the field to the custom report type field layout.

sourceExplanation: Add the field to the custom report type field layout is the correct solution because fields from objects in unmanaged packages are not automatically available in existing custom report types. To make the new field appear as a column in the report, the app builder must edit the custom report type and add the field to the report type’s layout. Why the other options are incorrect: • Adjust the field level security to include in the report type: Field-level security controls visibility of fields to users, but if the field is not included in the report type layout, it still won’t appear as an available column. • Check Allow Reports for the position and applicant objects: This setting controls whether the object itself is reportable. Since the report already exists, the objects are confirmed to be reportable. • Update the profile with the Manage Public Reports permission: This permission allows managing public reports but does not add fields from the object to the report type's available field set.

stem: Sales Managers want to be automatically notified any time there is a change to an Opportunity Close Date and want these changes to be tracked on the Opportunity. Which two configurations should an app builder recommend?

options.text: Use a record-triggered flow on Opportunity and a Chatter post action.

sourceExplanation: The correct solutions are Use a record-triggered flow on Opportunity and a Chatter post action and Enable Feed Tracking on Opportunities. The record-triggered flow can detect the specific field change and post a notification to Chatter to alert the Sales Managers. Enabling Feed Tracking for the Close Date field will ensure the change is recorded and visible in the Opportunity's feed, providing the required tracking history. Why the other options are incorrect: • Create an Opportunity outbound message: While an outbound message can send a notification, it is an older technology primarily for integrations and does not inherently track the change on the record itself. • Activate Historical Trending for Opportunities: This feature tracks field history for reporting over time, but it does not provide automatic, real-time notifications to managers when a change occurs.

stem: Universal Container's sales reps can modify fields on an opportunity until it is closed. The sales operations team has access to modify the Post-Close Follow-up Date and Post-Close Follow-up Comments fields after the opportunity is closed. After the opportunity is closed, the rest of the fields are read only. How should these requirements be met?

options.text: Use field-level security to mark fields as read-only on the Sales profile.
Use field-level security on page layouts with record types to restrict editing fields.
Use record types with field sets and restrict editing fields using field-level security.
Use field-level security on page layouts to restrict editing fields.

sourceExplanation: Use field-level security on page layouts with record types to restrict editing fields is the correct solution. This scenario requires different field-level access based on the record's stage (Open vs. Closed). The app builder should create two record types (e.g., "Open Opportunity" and "Closed Opportunity") with distinct page layouts. Field-Level Security (FLS) on these page layouts can then be configured to make most fields read-only on the "Closed Opportunity" layout while keeping the specific follow-up fields editable for the sales operations team's profile. Why the other options are incorrect: • Use field-level security to mark fields as read-only on the Sales profile: FLS on a profile is static and applies universally; it cannot change a field from editable to read-only based on a record's status like the Stage. • Use record types with field sets and restrict editing fields using field-level security: Field sets organize fields on a page layout but do not control editability based on record state. FLS itself, without the conditional logic provided by record types and layouts, is insufficient. • Use field-level security on page layouts to restrict editing fields: This is partially correct, but without using record types to swap the layout when the opportunity is closed, there is no mechanism to change which layout (and thus which field permissions) is applied.
